item.title: Friends and Family Contributions to Individual Trump Accounts Cross the $1 Billion Mark
item.description:
Press Release:            November 24, 2026

Contact:                     Treasury Public Affairs, Press@treasury.gov

Friends and Family Contributions to Individual Trump Accounts Cross the $1 Billion Mark

WASHINGTON — Trump Accounts today announced that contributions from friends and family members to individual accounts have surpassed $1 billion—a historic milestone in the effort to give every American child a stronger financial future.

This billion-dollar milestone was made possible by contributions from more than 3 million friends and family members—independent of the major philanthropic gifts from donors such as the Michael & Susan Dell Foundation. Commitments from friends and families, philanthropists, and the $1,000 seed donation from the U.S. Department of the Treasury bring total assets deposited in Trump Accounts to over $9 billion.

“Trump Accounts are a transformative government program for American children. It is the largest government start-up in American history. Adding to this effort is the extraordinary response from friends and family members of individual Trump Account holders, whose contributions have now surpassed $1 billion nationwide,” said Frank J. Bisignano, Chief Executive Officer of the Internal Revenue Service. “Parents should download the Trump Accounts app today and claim their child’s account to watch their financial future grow.”

“The American people are investing in Trump Accounts with a generosity that represents the finest instincts of our national character,” said Secretary of the Treasury Scott Bessent. “President Trump wanted to make it especially easy to contribute to Trump Accounts, and friends and families across the country are seizing that opportunity to help the next generation build wealth from day one. This week, the President himself joined the millions of Americans who have made personal donations to individual Trump Accounts. With every contribution, we are bringing the promise of long-term financial security within reach of American children from every kind of family and every kind of background.”

Friends and families can contribute directly to children’s Trump Accounts once they are claimed by using the QR code feature found in the child’s Trump Accounts app.

Trump Accounts are tax-advantaged investment accounts for American children under the age of eighteen established under the Working Families Tax Cuts. The U.S. Department of the Treasury has opened a Trump Account for every eligible child with a valid Social Security number, creating a pathway for philanthropic contributions to invest in the financial futures of millions of American children.

Children born between January 1, 2025, and December 31, 2028, are also eligible to receive a one-time $1,000 seed contribution from the U.S. Department of the Treasury. 

A parent or guardian must claim their child’s Trump Account to manage it and allow for family members, friends, and employers to contribute.

To claim a child’s Trump Account, parents or guardians should download the official Trump Accounts app available in the Apple App Store and Google Play. During the claiming process, a parent or guardian will verify their identity and relationship to their child, review the child’s information, and accept the account terms.

Once the child’s account is claimed, friends and families can contribute up to $5,000 per year, and employers can contribute up to $2,500 per year, subject to the $5,000 per year limit.

To learn more about Trump Accounts, visit TrumpAccounts.gov.

item.title: Treasury Identifies Nearly $15 Billion in Potential Iranian Shadow Banking
item.description:
U.S. Department of the Treasury

Office of Public Affairs

Press Release:            November 23, 2026

Contact:                     Treasury Public Affairs, Press@treasury.gov

Treasury Identifies Nearly $15 Billion in Potential Iranian Shadow Banking

WASHINGTON— In a new Financial Trend Analysis, the U.S. Department of the Treasury’s Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN) identified approximately $14.7 billion of financial activity from January 2025 to August 2026 potentially linked to Iranian shadow banking. As part of their compliance requirements, U.S. financial institutions flag suspicious activity to FinCEN, making it available to law enforcement and national security agencies.

“Financial institutions are often the first line of defense in denying Iranian regime-linked funds access to the U.S. economy,” said Secretary of the Treasury Scott Bessent. “Treasury will continue to sever the financial lifelines on which the regime relies to fund its military, weapons programs, and terror proxies.”

The trends and methods associated with potential Iranian shadow banking remained relatively consistent through 2026. Potential Iranian shadow banking networks continue to be connected across continents, most prominently in the United Arab Emirates (UAE), Hong Kong, and Singapore, and by the oil, shipping, investment, technology procurement, and other industries.

KEY FINDINGS

  • The most common routes for funds flagged by financial institutions were:
    • from mainland China-based banks to UAE-based banks: approximately $2.6 billion;
    • Singapore-based banks to UAE-based banks: approximately $981 million; and
    • United Kingdom-based banks to UAE-based banks: approximately $922 million.
  • The potential exploitation of companies registered in the Marshall Islands and British Virgin Islands, usually at addresses linked to corporate registries, emerged as an area of concern.
  • Potential Iran-linked companies were involved in a diverse array of businesses, including shipping, trading, and oil.

REPORTING SUSPICIOUS IRAN-RELATED ACTIVITY

To support financial institutions in their Bank Secrecy Act reporting, FinCEN has previously issued several publications that highlight red flags on Iran-linked actors:

  • FinCEN Advisory on the Iranian Regime’s Illicit Oil Smuggling Activities, Shadow Banking Networks, and Weapons Procurement Efforts (June 2025)
  • FinCEN Alert on the Use of Front Companies, Financial Facilitators, and Digital Asset Infrastructure by Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps to Evade Sanctions and Launder Proceeds (May 2026)
  • FinCEN Alert to Counter Iranian Procurement Efforts for its Commercial Aviation Industry (September 2026)
  • FinCEN Alert to Counter Iranian Abuse of Religious Charity Networks (October 2026)

Through its whistleblower incentive program, FinCEN welcomes tips on Iran-related illicit finance. Individuals located in the United States or abroad who provide information about sanctions violations may be eligible for an award if the information they provide leads to a successful enforcement action that results in monetary penalties exceeding $1,000,000. As highlighted in FinCEN’s recent Bulletin (available in several languages), this includes information about violations of the Bank Secrecy Act or Office of Foreign Assets Control-administered sanctions programs that may involve the use of Iranian proxies and facilitators operating outside of Iran.

item.title: Operation Economic Outcast Disrupts Iran’s Global Shadow Banking Networks
item.description:
U.S. Department of the Treasury

Office of Public Affairs

Press Release:            November 23, 2026

Contact:                     Treasury Public Affairs, Press@treasury.gov

Operation Economic Outcast Disrupts Iran’s Global Shadow Banking Networks

WASHINGTON— Today, as part of Operation Economic Outcast, the U.S. Department of the Treasury sanctioned over two dozen Iranian exchange houses, front companies, and key personnel in a sweeping effort to disrupt Iran’s global shadow banking networks.  As Iran’s economy remains battered by punishing economic sanctions and its oil revenues continue to decline, the regime’s shadow banking facilitators have increasingly failed to repatriate dwindling export earnings while simultaneously enriching themselves by stealing state resources that rightfully belong to the Iranian people.

“Iran’s economy is underwater, and its leaders are panicking,” said Secretary of the Treasury Scott Bessent. “Iran’s shadow banking system is the last financial lifeline of a bankrupt regime. Treasury will continue dismantling these illicit networks until we have buried the head of the snake.”

Today’s action targets the financial infrastructure that underpins much of Iran’s remaining foreign trade, disrupting the exchange houses, front companies, and facilitators that move billions of dollars through the international financial system to provide the regime access to foreign currency despite comprehensive sanctions.

This action is being taken pursuant to the following Executive Orders (E.O.):  E.O. 13902, which targets certain sectors of the Iranian economy, including Iran’s financial sector; E.O. 13224, as amended, a counter-terrorism designation authority; and E.O. 13871, which targets persons operating in various sectors of Iran’s metals industry.  

OPERATION ECONOMIC OUTCAST IS ISOLATING THE IRANIAN REGIME

Announced by Secretary Bessent on August 24, 2026, dubbed Economic D-Day, Operation Economic Outcast is severing the remaining economic lifelines that sustain the Iranian regime.  Treasury has mapped the networks, facilitators, and financial channels that Iran uses to smuggle oil, evade sanctions, and fund terror.  Working with partners across the U.S. government, the European Union, United Kingdom, Gulf partners, and others, Treasury is targeting any source of the regime’s illicit revenue, as well as its sanctions evasion schemes to move funds.

Operation Economic Outcast significantly expanded sanctions risk for those who continue to choose to do business with Iran.  Treasury warned that any entity facilitating money laundering or sanctions evasion on behalf of Iran risks being cut off from the U.S. financial system.  It also expanded secondary sanctions exposure for those who continue doing business with the Iranian regime and will accelerate the pace of U.S. enforcement.  More information on Operation Economic Outcast is available here.  

EXCHANGE HOUSES AND RAHBAR COMPANIES

Iran’s shadow banking system is overseen by the Central Bank of Iran and relies on dozens of Iran-based exchange houses and “rahbar companies,” bank affiliates that manage sanctions evasion networks for their Iran-based clients.  Exchange houses and rahbar companies work hand-in-hand to facilitate the financial underpinnings of Iran’s international trade through thousands of front companies in multiple jurisdictions, most prominently, but not exclusively, in Dubai and Hong Kong.  Billions of dollars move through the international financial system in this fashion, sustaining the last remnants of Iran’s foreign trade.

Iran-based Rahbar Bazargani Nesim Baharan Qeshm Company (Nesim Baharan) operates as the rahbar company for Bank Sarmayeh and works closely with Iranian exchange houses and their front companies to facilitate transactions on behalf of Bank Sarmayeh’s Iranian clients, which include major Iranian petrochemical companies.  Sayyed Mohammad Jalali, Valiollah Hemmati, and Ali Kalhor act as senior officials of Nesim Baharan.

Rahbar Bazargani Nesim Baharan Qeshm Company is being designated pursuant to E.O. 13902 for operating in the financial sector of the Iranian economy.  Sayyed Mohammad Jalali, Valiollah Hemmati, and Ali Kalhor are being designated pursuant to E.O. 13902 for having acted or purported to act for or on behalf of, directly or indirectly, Rahbar Bazargani Nesim Baharan Qeshm Company.

Iran-based Mina Fashki and Partners Exchange Company (Fashki Exchange) and Mellat Exchange Company are exchange houses operating within Iran’s shadow banking system.  Mina Fashki and Farzad Fashki own and operate Fashki Exchange, while Mahmoud Akhlaghi, Parviz Fazlju, and Mohammad Hossein Abbasi are officials of Mellat Exchange Company.

Note 1: This graphic updates an April 2026 version to include Bank Sarmayeh and its rahbar.

Fashki Exchange and Mellat Exchange Company are being designated pursuant to E.O. 13902 for operating in the financial sector of the Iranian economy.  Mina Fashki and Farzad Fashki are being designated pursuant to E.O. 13902 for having acted or purported to act for or on behalf of, directly or indirectly, Fashki Exchange.  Mahmoud Akhlaghi, Parviz Fazlju, and Mohammad Hossein Abbasi are being designated pursuant to E.O. 13902 for having acted or purported to act for or on behalf of, directly or indirectly, Mellat Exchange Company.

Dubai-based Grand Target Heavy Equipment and Machinery Spare Parts Trading L.L.C, Recaz Star General Trading LLC, Meethale Raw Materials Trading Company LLC, Hemraj Trading L.L.C,  Ewan Al Madeena General Trading LLC, OGA Global General Trading L.L.C, Dexterous Global DMCC, Khore Al Hilal Goods Wholesalers Trading LLC, Türkiye-based Bogazici Gumrukleme Ithalat Ihracat Turizm Petrol Urunleri Sanayi Ve Ticaret Limited Sirketi, and Hong Kong-based Grandez Trading Limited are exchange house front companies used by Iran’s rahbar network to facilitate thousands of cross-border payments, worth billions of dollars, on behalf of Iranian clients.  

These front companies have enabled Iran to carry out thousands of financial transactions through the rahbar network.  Khore Al Hilal Goods Wholesalers Trading LLC has been used extensively by U.S.-sanctioned Iranian exchange houses Opal Exchange, also known as Pedram Pirouzan Exchange, and Omid Sepah Exchange to move millions of dollars for Iranian Bank Sepah.  Grandez Trading Limited is a front company used by the U.S.-sanctioned Iranian exchange house Mohsen Khandan and Partners Exchange.  Recaz Star General Trading LLC has sent and received hundreds of payments totaling over $170 million from persons associated with Sadaf Exchange.  OGA Global General Trading LLC has overseen millions of dollars’ worth of payments for the National Iranian Tanker Company, which operates Iran’s fleet of state-owned oil tankers.

Grand Target Heavy Equipment and Machinery Spare Parts Trading L.L.C, Recaz Star General Trading LLC, Meethale Raw Materials Trading Company LLC, Hemraj Trading L.L.C,  Ewan Al Madeena General Trading LLC, OGA Global General Trading L.L.C,  Dexterous Global DMCC, Khore Al Hilal Goods Wholesalers Trading LLC, Bogazici Gumrukleme Ithalat Ihracat Turizm Petrol Urunleri Sanayi Ve Ticaret Limited Sirketi, and Grandez Trading Limited are being designated pursuant to E.O. 13902 for operating in the financial sector of the Iranian economy.  

SHADOW BANKING FRONT COMPANIES

Iranian exchange houses and rahbar companies operate through a multi-jurisdictional web of layered front and shell companies that enable them to remit and receive payments overseas on behalf of their Iranian customers.  Iranian companies that participate in the global economy, in some way or fashion, engage with the Iranian shadow banking system to facilitate imports and exports.  For example, Dubai-based Robust Trading LLC has facilitated payments for the sanctioned Iran-based copper mining giant National Iranian Copper Industries Company.  Similarly, HMS Trading FZE, the Dubai-based oil export and commercial front company of Iranian Shahr Bank, has used Dubai-based Integral Petro Energy Trading LLC to facilitate millions of dollars’ worth of liquefied petroleum gas sales by Iranian petrochemical exporter Kharg Petrochemical Company Limited.

Robust Trading LLC is being designated pursuant to E.O. 13871 for having materially assisted, sponsored, or provided financial, material, or technological support for, or goods or services in support of, the National Iranian Copper Industries Company.  Integral Petro Energy Trading LLC is being designated pursuant to E.O. 13902 for having materially assisted, sponsored, or provided financial, material, or technological support for, or goods or services to or in support of, HMS Trading FZE.

 

Other Dubai-based front companies include Royah Altahabia Trading L.L.C, Alam Al Sahra Building Materials Trading Co. L.L.C, Berkeley Trading LLC, and Nordic International Trading LLC, which have been counterparties to millions of dollars’ worth of transactions involving Iranian financial broker front companies operating within Iran’s rahbar system.  Since at least 2022, Berkeley Trading L.L.C has facilitated millions of dollars’ worth of transactions for clients of Iran-based Amin Exchange.

Royah Altahabia Trading L.L.C, Alam Al Sahra Building Materials Trading Co. L.L.C, Berkeley Trading LLC, and Nordic International Trading LLC are being designated pursuant to E.O. 13902 for operating in the financial sector of the Iranian economy. 

Dubai-based Gespl International General Trading LLC has been used by the National Iranian Oil Company as part of its oil and petrochemicals sales mechanism and is actively involved in money laundering via Iran’s shadow banking mechanism.   

Gespl International General Trading LLC is being designated pursuant to E.O. 13902 for operating in the petrochemical sector of the Iranian economy. 

Iran’s military organs also utilize the shadow banking system.  Iranian Armed Forces General Staff-associated Sepehr Energy Jahan Nama Pars Company (SEJ) and sanctioned shipping company Dragon Road Ltd utilized Dubai-based H N B Trading Co LLC to complete payment for the charter of the SERENE I (IMO 9197832); H N B Trading Co LLC received hundreds of thousands of dollars from a SEJ front company as part of this scheme.

H N B Trading Co LLC is being designated pursuant to E.O. 13224, as amended, for having materially assisted, sponsored, or provided financial, material, or technological support for, or goods or services to or in support of, Sepehr Energy Jahan Nama Pars Company.

IRAN CENTER FOR EXCHANGE

Additionally, as part of today’s action, OFAC is taking action against the Iran-based Iran Center for Exchange of Currency and Gold (Iran Center for Exchange), which plays an essential intermediary role within Iran’s system of international trade.  The Iran Center for Exchange provides the financial plumbing to match exporters, who earn foreign currency from sales abroad, to importers, who need foreign currency to purchase goods, for tens of billions of dollars’ worth of trade every year.  While Iran’s shadow banking system moves the funds generated by Iran’s international trade, the Iran Center for Exchange plays matchmaker and guides these funds to their ultimate destination inside Iran.  The Central Bank of Iran also utilizes bonds issued by the Iran Center for Exchange to help facilitate international trade using Russian roubles and Chinese yuan without reliance on the U.S. dollar.  

The Iran Center for Exchange is being designated pursuant to E.O. 13902 for operating in the financial sector of the Iranian economy.  

SANCTIONS IMPLICATIONS

As a result of today’s OFAC action, all property and interests in property of the designated or blocked persons described above that are in the United States or in the possession or control of U.S. persons are blocked and must be reported to OFAC.  In addition, any entities that are owned, directly or indirectly, individually or in the aggregate, 50 percent or more by one or more blocked persons are also blocked.   OFAC’s regulations generally prohibit all transactions, unless authorized by a general or specific license issued by OFAC, or exempt, by U.S. persons or within (or transiting) the United States that involve any property or interests in property of blocked persons.  

Violations of U.S. sanctions may result in the imposition of civil or criminal penalties on U.S. and foreign persons.  OFAC may impose civil penalties for sanctions violations on a strict liability basis.  OFAC’s Economic Sanctions Enforcement Guidelines provide more information regarding OFAC’s enforcement of U.S. economic sanctions.  The prohibitions include the making of any contribution or provision of funds, goods, or services by, to, or for the benefit of any designated or blocked person, or the receipt of any contribution or provision of funds, goods, or services from any such person.  Non-U.S. persons are also prohibited from causing U.S. persons to wittingly or unwittingly violate U.S. sanctions, as well as engaging in conduct that evades or conspires to violate U.S. sanctions.  Individuals located in the U.S. or abroad who provide information about sanctions violations to FinCEN’s whistleblower incentive program may be eligible for awards if the information they provide leads to a successful enforcement action that results in monetary penalties exceeding $1,000,000.   

Financial institutions and other persons may risk exposure to sanctions for engaging in certain transactions or activities with designated or otherwise blocked persons, including the persons designated today.  This includes, in addition to blocking prohibitions, that OFAC can prohibit or impose strict conditions on opening or maintaining, in the United States, a correspondent account or a payable-through account of a foreign financial institution that knowingly conducts or facilitates any significant transaction on behalf of a person who is designated pursuant to the relevant authority.  

The power and integrity of OFAC sanctions derive not only from OFAC’s ability to designate and add persons to the SDN List, but also from its willingness to remove persons from the SDN List, when consistent with relevant statutes and other authorities.  The ultimate goal of sanctions is to bring about a positive change in behavior.  What constitutes a sufficient change in circumstance will vary based on context, including the status of the broader geopolitical circumstances affecting the national security and foreign policy interests implicated by the declared national emergency.  In the case of sanctions related to Iran, OFAC is employing all available statutory, regulatory, and policy tools to resolve the persistent national emergencies posed by Iran, which has not changed its behavior to align with U.S. national security and foreign policy objectives.  OFAC sanctions determinations, including removal determinations, are made consistent with Administration foreign policy and national security policies and priorities.  For more information concerning the process for seeking removal from an OFAC list, including the SDN List, or to submit a request, please refer to OFAC’s guidance on How to Request Removal from an OFAC List.

item.title: Operation Economic Outcast Targets Corrupt Regime Insiders Exploiting Iran’s Oil Sector for Personal Gain

U.S. Department of the Treasury

Office of Public Affairs

Press Release:            November 20, 2026

Contact:                     Treasury Public Affairs, Press@treasury.gov

Operation Economic Outcast Targets Corrupt Regime Insiders Exploiting Iran’s Oil Sector for Personal Gain

WASHINGTON—Today, as part of Operation Economic Outcast, the U.S. Department of the Treasury is targeting key “oil trustees” the Iranian regime relies on to facilitate the sale of oil abroad. With no oil on the water outside of the U.S. military blockade and no oil loaded onto vessels since the start of Operation Economic Outcast, the regime is attempting to recoup billions of dollars from its oil trustees.  In many cases, these corrupt trustees have kept the oil revenue for personal gain.

“Iran’s tyrannical regime never fails to put its own interests before those of its own citizens, even as ordinary Iranians face shortages of bread and fuel,” said Secretary of the Treasury Scott Bessent.  “The regime has exhausted its seaborne oil supply, and it may never see the revenue from the oil it has already sold. The ship is sinking.”

The designations imposed today are being taken pursuant to Executive Order (E.O.) 13902, which targets the Iranian petroleum, petrochemical, and aviation sectors, among other key sectors of the Iranian economy, and E.O. 13224, as amended, a counterterrorism authority.

UNTRUSTWORTHY TRUSTEES

Mohammad Javad Bavand (Bavand) and Majid Taj (Taj), the brother of the Iranian Football Federation’s president, operate as part of a network of regime insiders tasked with obtaining desperately needed cash by selling from Iran’s dwindling oil reserves.  Bavand, a former IRGC intelligence officer, has spearheaded this effort, entrusting a group of personal contacts, including Taj, to recoup Iran’s oil funds located in third countries.  The Iranian regime continues to entrust Bavand and Taj’s network with facilitating Iran’s oil sales, despite members owing billions of dollars to the regime from previous sales.  Bavand has worked with a variety of illicit oil trading actors, including the IRGC and Sepehr Energy Jahan Nama Pars Company (SEJ), a U.S.-designated front company tasked with selling oil for the Iranian Armed Forces General Staff. 

Mohammad Javad Bavand and Majid Taj are being designated pursuant to E.O. 13902 for operating in the petroleum sector of the Iranian economy.

Mohammadhossein Servati is being designated pursuant to E.O. 13224, as amended, for having materially assisted, sponsored, or provided financial, material, or technological support for, or goods or services to or in support of, Sepehr Energy Jahan Nama Pars Company. 

Mojtaba Arabnejad (Mojtaba) is the son of the designated Iranian businessman and CEO of Iran’s Mahan Air, Hamid Arabnejad.  Using his familial ties and special connections with the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps-Qods Force (IRGC-QF), Mojtaba has been involved in purchasing aircraft parts for Mahan Air and procuring weapons for the Iranian military under the auspices of agricultural companies.  Like others designated today, Mojtaba has overseen oil sales for the Iranian regime, the proceeds from which have supported Mahan Air.

item.title: Treasury Sanctions Major Drug Trafficking Organizations Supporting Terrorist Cartels
item.description:
U.S. Department of the Treasury

Office of Public Affairs

Press Release:            November 19, 2026

Contact:                     Treasury Public Affairs, Press@treasury.gov

Treasury Sanctions Major Drug Trafficking Organizations Supporting Terrorist Cartels

Coordinated Action with International Partners Targets a Cartel-Linked Outlaw Motorcycle Gang and Canadian-Based Mafia Leaders and Facilitators 

WASHINGTON—Today, the Department of the Treasury’s Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) sanctioned two international drug trafficking organizations: the Australia-headquartered Comanchero Outlaw Motorcycle Gang (Comancheros) and the Italy-based ‘Ndrangheta, a mafia-type criminal syndicate.  By providing essential logistical and operational support, the Comancheros and ‘Ndrangheta help terrorist cartels expand their international reach and sustain global narcotrafficking networks.

“Cartels do not operate in isolation. They rely on other criminal organizations like the Comancheros and ‘Ndrangheta to move drugs, launder illicit proceeds, and ultimately poison Americans with narcotics,” said Secretary of the Treasury Scott Bessent.  “Treasury will continue to expose and disrupt narcoterrorism networks to Keep America Safe.”

The Comancheros and the ‘Ndrangheta operate sophisticated transnational criminal networks that facilitate large-scale drug trafficking and money laundering. The ‘Ndrangheta controls a significant share of the European cocaine trade, while the Comancheros have helped open access to some of the world's most lucrative illicit drug markets.

In keeping with President Trump’s pledge to eliminate cartels, OFAC has prioritized targeting these and other criminal groups that threaten the welfare of Americans. Treasury has coordinated closely with the Homeland Security Task Force (HSTF), taking nearly 40 actions against over 500 individuals and entities since the beginning of 2025.  OFAC uses a network-based approach to simultaneously disrupt as many different facets of the cartels as possible, from their leadership and key organizational nodes to facilitators and enablers, such as corrupt officials, complicit family members, and ostensibly legitimate front persons.

Today’s action reflects a unified, whole-of-government effort to ensure operational coordination and maximize impact against transnational criminal networks.  OFAC conducted its investigation in parallel with the HSTF, with support from the Federal Bureau of Investigation, Drug Enforcement Administration, and Homeland Security Investigations.  OFAC continues to work closely with the HSTF to disrupt the flow of illicit drugs and dismantle the networks, facilitators, and financial infrastructure that enable their production and distribution. 

Additionally, OFAC worked closely with valued international partners, including the Australian Federal Police, New Zealand Police, Italy’s Guardia di Finanza, and Canada’s Royal Canadian Mounted Police and York Regional Police, whose cooperation was instrumental in supporting today’s action.

The action was taken pursuant to Executive Order (E.O.) 14059, which targets the proliferation of illicit drugs and their means of production.

COMANCHERO OUTLAW MOTORCYCLE GANG

Today, OFAC designated the Comancheros, also known as the Comanchero Motorcycle Club or simply Comanchero MC, an Australian drug trafficking organization with an international footprint in Asia, Europe, and North America.  Developing strategic partnerships with U.S. sanctioned cartels, including the Sinaloa Cartel, CJNG, Clan del Golfo, and Los Choneros, the Comancheros have facilitated multi-hundred-kilogram shipments of cocaine from South America to the United States, Australia, and Europe.  The Comancheros have also been involved in other criminal activity around the world, including assassinations, arms trafficking, and money laundering.

Because Australia and New Zealand are some of the world’s most lucrative illicit drug markets, Mexican cartels are increasingly targeting these markets to capitalize on the significantly higher margins and growing demand.  Due to the geographic distance from the major cocaine producing regions in the Western Hemisphere, cartels can charge substantial premiums compared to drugs sold in the United States.  The Sinaloa Cartel has been known to send “sleeper cells” to Australia to facilitate local drug distribution and establish contacts with the Comancheros and other outlaw motorcycle gangs who assist with the logistics of drug trafficking.

 

The Comancheros are being designated under E.O. 14059 for having engaged in, or having attempted to engage in, activities or transactions that have materially contributed to, or pose a significant risk of materially contributing to, the international proliferation of illicit drugs or their means of production.

 

COMANCHERO COMMAND AND CONTROL

Alexandre Varela Villar, better known as Alex Vare (Vare), is the Spain-based World Commander of the Comancheros.

Allan John Norman Meehan, better known as Allan Meehan (Meehan), is the Australia-based World President of the Comancheros.

Pasilika Naufahu (Pasilika) is the national president of the New Zealand chapter of the Comancheros.  Before being deported to New Zealand in 2016, Pasilika was the sergeant-at-arms of the Comancheros in Australia.  Pasilika was arrested and sentenced to 10 years in prison in February 2021 for various charges related to his position in the Comancheros.  In close coordination with his brother and senior Comancheros member, Vetekina Naufahu (Vetekina), Pasilika has facilitated multi-hundred-kilogram importations of drugs into New Zealand and has established connections to the Sinaloa Cartel. 

Marco Francis Coffen (Coffen) is an associate of the Comancheros and has been involved in supplying multiple Australian criminal organizations, including the Comancheros, with encrypted communication platforms to drug traffickers and shielding them from police phone taps.

Vare and Meehan are being designated pursuant to E.O. 14059 for being or having been leaders or officials of the Comancheros.

Pasilika and Vetekina are being designated pursuant to E.O. 14059 for having acted or purported to act for or on behalf of, directly or indirectly, the Comancheros.

Coffen is being designated pursuant to E.O. 14059 for having provided, or attempted to provide, financial, material, or technological support for, or goods or services in support of, the Comancheros.

OMERTÀ – THE ‘NDRANGHETA

The ‘Ndrangheta, an international drug trafficking organization and mafia-type criminalsyndicate, operates in over 80 countries and continues to grow.  The ‘Ndrangheta’s adherence to omertà, a code of silence, and its reliance on deeply rooted familial bloodlines have enabled the organization to maintain secrecy, foster loyalty, resist infiltration, and expand its criminal influence across generations and international borders.  While the ‘Ndrangheta was founded in Calabria, Italy, the organization has expanded across Europe, the Western Hemisphere, and Australia.  As one of the largest criminal organizations in the world, the ‘Ndrangheta’s primary business comes from drug trafficking, with some estimates stating that almost 80 percent of the European cocaine trade is controlled by the ‘Ndrangheta.  While primarily focused on the cocaine trade, Italian officials have stated that the ‘Ndrangheta have started expanding into the illicit fentanyl market. 

The ’Ndrangheta frequently partner with Mexican and South American drug trafficking organizations and FTOs, including the Sinaloa Cartel, CJNG, and Clan del Golfo.  In the past, the ‘Ndrangheta has also partnered with other Mexican drug trafficking organizations and FTOs, including Los Zetas (now known as Cartel del Noreste) and the Gulf Cartel.    

The ‘Ndrangheta was previously designated on May 30, 2008, pursuant to the Foreign Narcotics Kingpin Designation Act (Kingpin Act).  Today, the ‘Ndrangheta is being designated pursuant to E.O. 14059 for having engaged in, or having attempted to engage in, activities or transactions that have materially contributed to, or pose a significant risk of materially contributing to, the international proliferation of illicit drugs or their means of production.

'NDRANGHETISTI NORTH OF THE BORDER

Locali (singular: locale) are the primary territorial organizational unit of the ‘Ndrangheta, comprising members known as ‘ndranghetisti, that oversee and coordinate criminal activities within a specific geographical region.  The ‘Ndrangheta locale that operates in the Greater Toronto Area in Canada has strengthened in recent years, becoming so powerful that they dictate events in Italy from across the ocean.  In Canada, the ‘Ndrangheta is involved in drug trafficking, money laundering, murder, and other crimes.  This faction of the ‘Ndrangheta uses the U.S. and Canadian financial systems to launder illicit proceeds.

Today, OFAC designated Italian-born Angelo Figliomeni (also known as “Don Angelino”), the leader of the Toronto faction of the ‘Ndrangheta.  A member of the Figliomeni ‘ndrina (family), Angelo Figliomeni fled to Canada in the early 2000’s to escape a 20-year sentence for weapons charges in Italy.  Angelo’s power extends beyond Canada, stretching back to Italy.  He has engaged in money laundering and other criminal activities on behalf of the ‘Ndrangheta. 

Another member of the Figliomeni ‘ndrina is Italian-born Cosimo Figliomeni (sometimes known as “Cosimino”), who is a top leader of the ‘Ndrangheta faction in Toronto and has been the subject of criminal proceedings in Italy in connection to his role within the ‘Ndrangheta organization.

OFAC also designated two members of the Commisso ‘ndrina who are long time Italian-born leaders of the ‘Ndrangheta in Toronto.  Francesco Commisso, also known as “U Scelto,” has faced allegations in Italy of being part of a Toronto oversight body that was tasked, among other duties, with imposing disciplinary sanctions on members. 

Rocco Remo Commisso (also known as Remo Commisso) is a Canada-based leader of the ‘Ndrangheta and leads narcotics trafficking networks within the United States, including in the state of New York.  Remo Commisso was convicted in Canada in 1981 for conspiracy to commit murder and again in 1984 for his involvement in a bombing that killed one person.  Remo Commisso is involved in narcotics trafficking in the United States for the ‘Ndrangheta, including in New York.  

Vincenzo DeMaria (also known as Jimmy DeMaria) is one of Toronto’s top ‘Ndrangheta bosses and has been active in the Toronto organized crime scene for decades.  DeMaria shot and killed a man in 1981 over a $2,000 drug debt and was convicted of second-degree murder in 1982.  He has since been released from prison and holds significant power in the ‘Ndrangheta.  Cosimo Figliomeni, Francesco Commisso, Remo Commisso, and Jimmy DeMaria make up the Camera di Controllo of Toronto, a collegial body of the ‘Ndrangheta that decides on important questions concerning the organization and settles disputes, even outside of Toronto.  The Toronto ‘Ndrangheta is tightly connected throughout the world and has close relationships with members back in Calabria.

Luigi Vescio Sr. (also known as “The Undertaker” or “Lui Vescio”) is a Canadian-born ‘Ndrangheta senior member and associate of Angelo Figliomeni and Jimmy DeMaria. 

Angelo Figliomeni, Cosimo Figliomeni, Francesco Commisso, Remo Commisso, and Luigi Vescio Sr. were all charged in the Italian Court of Reggio Calabria for mafia-type association related to their leadership, membership, and promotion of the ‘Ndrangheta in 2019. 

Angelo Figliomeni, Cosimo Figliomeni, Francesco Commisso, Remo Commisso, Jimmy DeMaria, and Luigi Vescio Sr. are being designated pursuant to E.O. 14059 for having acted or purported to act for or on behalf of, directly or indirectly, ‘Ndrangheta.

FAMILY-OWNED, MAFIA-CONNECTED – VESCIO FUNERAL HOMES

OFAC is also designating the corporate network of Vescio Sr., including his network of funeral homes in Ontario.  These funeral homes include the Fratelli Vescio Funeral Homes Ltd. in Woodbridge, Ontario, Vescio Funeral Homes Ltd. in Toronto and Vescio Funeral Home (Maple) Inc. in Maple, Ontario.  Vescio Sr. also controls a Toronto-based luxury limousine rental business, Phantom Limousine Services Inc.  Vescio Sr. serves as the president of each of these companies. 

OFAC is also designating Luigi Vescio Sr.’s wife, Rose Vescio, and his two children, Luigi Vescio Jr. and Laura Vescio, for their roles in owning and operating the Vescio Funeral Homes on behalf of Luigi Vescio Sr. 

Rose Vescio, Luigi Vescio Jr., and Laura Vescio are being designated pursuant to E.O. 14059 for having acted or purported to act for or on behalf of, directly or indirectly, Luigi Vescio Sr.

SANCTIONS IMPLICATIONS

As a result of today’s action, all property and interests in property of the designated or blocked persons described above that are in the United States or in the possession or control of U.S. persons are blocked and must be reported to OFAC.  In addition, any entities that are owned, directly or indirectly, individually or in the aggregate, 50 percent or more by one or more blocked persons are also blocked.  Unless authorized by a general or specific license issued by OFAC, or exempt, OFAC’s regulations generally prohibit all transactions by U.S. persons or within (or transiting) the United States that involve any property or interests in property of blocked persons.

Violations of U.S. sanctions may result in the imposition of civil or criminal penalties on U.S. and foreign persons.  OFAC may impose civil penalties for sanctions violations on a strict liability basis.  OFAC’s Economic Sanctions Enforcement Guidelines provide more information regarding OFAC’s enforcement of U.S. economic sanctions.  In addition, financial institutions and other persons may risk exposure to sanctions for engaging in certain transactions or activities involving designated or otherwise blocked persons.  The prohibitions include the making of any contribution or provision of funds, goods, or services by, to, or for the benefit of any designated or blocked person, or the receipt of any contribution or provision of funds, goods, or services from any such person.

Furthermore, engaging in certain transactions involving the persons designated today may risk the imposition of secondary sanctions on participating foreign financial institutions.  OFAC can prohibit or impose strict conditions on opening or maintaining, in the United States, a correspondent account or a payable-through account of a foreign financial institution that knowingly conducts or facilitates any significant transaction on behalf of a person who is designated pursuant to the relevant authority.

The power and integrity of OFAC sanctions derive not only from OFAC’s ability to designate and add persons to the Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List (SDN List), but also from its willingness to remove persons from the SDN List consistent with the law.  The ultimate goal of sanctions is not to punish, but to bring about a positive change in behavior.  For information concerning the process for seeking removal from an OFAC list, including the SDN List, or to submit a request, please refer to OFAC’s guidance on Filing a Petition for Removal from an OFAC List.

item.description:
U.S. Department of the Treasury

Office of Public Affairs

Press Release:            November 19, 2026

Contact:                     Treasury Public Affairs, Press@treasury.gov

Treasury Targets Cyber Scam Operators and Armed Group Facilitators in Southeast Asia

WASHINGTON—Today, the U.S. Department of the Treasury’s Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) sanctioned three individuals involved in operating and facilitating cyber scam centers in Southeast Asia, as well as two affiliated companies.  The individuals designated today include operators of scam compounds that target Americans through virtual currency investment fraud and affiliates of armed groups that provide protection and support to scam-center networks in Southeast Asia.  

“Under President Trump’s leadership, Treasury has aggressively targeted overseas scam compounds to protect Americans from fraud,” said Secretary of the Treasury Scott Bessent.  “We will continue to use all available tools to disrupt and dismantle the networks that enable scam compounds to operate.”

These actions are being taken in furtherance of President Trump’s Executive Order (E.O.) 14390 of March 6, 2026, “Combating Cybercrime, Fraud, and Predatory Schemes Against American Citizens,” which orders the U.S. Government to unleash every available tool to stop foreign-backed criminal networks that exploit vulnerable Americans through cybercrime, cyber-enabled fraud, and extortion.  Today’s action further reflects OFAC’s coordination with the Federal Bureau of Investigation’s New York Field Office, Department of Justice’s Scam Center Strike Force, and the Drug Enforcement Administration, and the Homeland Security Task Force and National Coordination Center.  OFAC is taking today’s actions pursuant to E.O. 13694, as amended by E.O. 13757, E.O. 14144, and E.O. 14306 (“E.O. 13694, as further amended”).

ZHAO HUI: A SCAM CENTER OPERATOR

Zhao Hui (Zhao) is a Cambodian national who leased a scam center owned by the OFAC-designated Prince Group TCO and paid protection fees to the OFAC-designated leader of the Prince Group TCO, Chen Zhi.  In addition,Zhao owned a scam compound in Cambodia independent of Prince Group TCO.  At this scam compound, Zhao was directly involved in scam operations and managed this scam compound’s leases.  This scam compound primarily targeted Americans and Europeans.  Such scam compounds conduct virtual currency investment scams.  Since Zhao has leased a scam compound and owned and operated an additional scam compound in Cambodia, he has materially assisted, sponsored, or provided financial, material, or technological support for, or goods or services to or in support of virtual cryptocurrency investment scams, an activity described in subsection 1(a)(ii) of E.O. 13694, as further amended.   

Zhao is being designated pursuant to E.O. 13694, as further amended, for having materially assisted, sponsored, or provided financial, material, or technological support for, or goods or services to or in support of, an activity described in subsection 1(a)(ii) of E.O. 13694, as further amended.  

Zhao is the chairman of the board of directors of Cambodia-based construction company Bei Fang Bo Lin Construction Decoration Co., Ltd. (Bei Fang Bo Lin) and management and consultancy company ZHZ Investment Consulting Co., Ltd. (ZHZ Investment).   

Bei Fang Bo Lin and ZHZ Investment are being designated pursuant to E.O. 13694, as further amended, for being owned or controlled by, or having acted or purported to act for or on behalf of, directly or indirectly, Zhao Hui.

THE DKBA’S FACILITATION OF SCAM COMPOUND ACTIVITY

In recent years, armed groups in Burma have transformed a strip along the Thai-Burmese border into one of the world’s highest concentrations of scam centers.  The Democratic Karen Benevolent Army (DKBA) is an ethnic armed group previously designated by OFAC for supporting cyber scam centers in Burma that target Americans using fraudulent investment schemes.  DKBA actors not only provide security for scam compounds and permit their continued operation, but also actively participate in violence against victims of human trafficking trapped inside the compounds.

Since December 2025, General Saw Shwe Wah has been the commander-in-chief of the DKBA, replacing General Saw Steel, who OFAC designated in November 2025 pursuant to E.O. 13694, as further amended. 

Colonel Saw A One is the DKBA commander who oversees security in the Three Pagodas Pass in Karen State near the Thai border.  The region has seen expansion of new buildings intended for telecom scam operations, with many scam actors entering the area with the assistance of the DKBA, which also protects them.  Saw A One reportedly owns a plantation where scam operations occur and has contracted for scam operations. 

Saw Shwe Wah and Saw A One are being designated pursuant to E.O. 13694, as further amended, for being or having been leaders, officials, senior executive officers, or members of the board of directors of the DKBA, a person whose property and interests in property are blocked pursuant to E.O. 13694, as further amended. 

SANCTIONS IMPLICATIONS

As a result of today’s action, all property and interests in property of the designated persons described above that are in the United States or in the possession or control of U.S. persons are blocked and must be reported to OFAC.  In addition, any entities that are owned, directly or indirectly, individually or in the aggregate, 50 percent or more by one or more blocked persons are also blocked.  Unless authorized by a general or specific license issued by OFAC, or exempt, OFAC’s regulations generally prohibit all transactions by U.S.  persons or within (or transiting) the United States that involve any property or interests in property of designated or otherwise blocked persons. 

Violations of U.S. sanctions may result in the imposition of civil or criminal penalties on U.S. and foreign persons.  OFAC may impose civil penalties for sanctions violations on a strict liability basis.  OFAC’s Economic Sanctions Enforcement Guidelines provide more information regarding OFAC’s enforcement of U.S. economic sanctions.  In addition, financial institutions and other persons may risk exposure to sanctions for engaging in certain transactions or activities involving designated or otherwise blocked persons.  The prohibitions include the making of any contribution or provision of funds, goods, or services by, to, or for the benefit of any designated or blocked person, or the receipt of any contribution or provision of funds, goods, or services from any such person.  Non-U.S. persons are also prohibited from causing or conspiring to cause U.S. persons to wittingly or unwittingly violate U.S. sanctions, as well as engaging in conduct that evades U.S. sanctions.  Individuals located in the U.S. or abroad who provide information about sanctions violations to FinCEN’s whistleblower incentive program may be eligible for awards if the information they provide leads to a successful enforcement action that results in monetary penalties exceeding $1,000,000.

Operation Economic Outcast Targets Iran’s Proxy Networks

Targets Include Hizballah-Affiliated Charity, Gold and Cash Smuggling Network

WASHINGTON— Today, the U.S. Department of the Treasury’s Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) designated the Wa Ta’awanu Association (Wa Ta’awanu), a Hizballah-affiliated charity that provides cover for Hizballah’s activities under the guise of delivering humanitarian services. Today’s action exposes Hizballah’s continued exploitation of civilian charitable organizations and its efforts to portray itself as a provider of humanitarian assistance.  It also increases pressure on the group’s illicit financing networks as Hizballah seeks to resist growing calls and international pressure to disarm.

Hassan Khechen and Ibrahim Khechen are being designated pursuant to E.O. 13224, as amended, for having materially assisted, sponsored, or provided financial, material, or technological support for, or goods or services to or in support of, Hizballah.  Gold Global Company and Sankari Gold is being designated pursuant to E.O. 13224, as amended, for being owned, controlled, or directed by, or for having acted or purported to act for or on behalf of, directly or indirectly, Hassan Khechen.

item.title: FinCEN Issues Proposed Rule to Strengthen Customer Due Diligence Requirements for Covered Financial Institutions
item.description:
U.S. Department of the Treasury

Office of Public Affairs

Press Release:            November 17, 2026

Contact:                     Treasury Public Affairs, Press@treasury.gov

FinCEN Issues Proposed Rule to Strengthen Customer Due Diligence Requirements for Covered Financial Institutions

WASHINGTON — Today, the U.S. Department of the Treasury’s Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN) issued a proposed rule to strengthen customer due diligence requirements, which are integral to efforts to combat money laundering and counter the financing of terrorism. FinCEN issues this proposal as a part of Treasury’s implementation of Executive Order 14406, Restoring Integrity to America’s Financial System.  

“Financial institutions are on the front lines of protecting our financial systems from criminal organizations and cartels that target law-abiding businesses and workers,” said Secretary of the Treasury Scott Bessent. “This proposed rule cuts unnecessary burden, gives institutions more flexibility to effectively combat risk, and strengthens our fight against financial crime.”

The proposed rule would amend customer due diligence requirements to:

  • explicitly provide that covered financial institutions can obtain additional information about beneficial owners of a legal entity customer that may be useful in mitigating risk or addressing supervisory concerns;
  • codify exceptive relief FinCEN issued removing the requirement for covered financial institutions to identify and verify the beneficial owners of a legal entity customer each time the customer opens a new account; and
  • specify information that a covered financial institution must obtain about each beneficial owner of a legal entity customer.

FinCEN welcomes public comments. The comment period closes 60 days after the proposed rule’s publication in the Federal Register.

item.title: Treasury, IRS Issue Final Rules to Help Hardworking Americans Build a Financially Secure Retirement
item.description:
U.S. Department of the Treasury

Office of Public Affairs

Press Release:            November 17, 2026

Contact:                     Treasury Public Affairs, Press@treasury.gov

Treasury, IRS Issue Final Rules to Help Hardworking Americans Build a Financially Secure Retirement

SECURE 2.0 Final Regulations Expand Automatic Enrollment in Workplace Retirement Plans

WASHINGTON — The U.S. Department of the Treasury and the Internal Revenue Service (IRS) today issued final regulations to help more Americans save for retirement through their workplaces. The regulations implement a key provision of the SECURE 2.0 Act, providing employers with clear guidance on automatic enrollment for certain 401(k) and 403(b) retirement plans. The rules help workers build retirement savings while preserving their control over how much they contribute. 

Treasury estimates that SECURE 2.0’s automatic enrollment expansion provision will increase retirement savings by an average of $4.2 billion annually over the 2023-2032 period.

“A financially secure retirement is a cornerstone of the American Dream, and every worker deserves the opportunity to achieve it,” said Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent. “Today’s rules help more American families and workers build retirement savings while keeping them in control of their contributions, and give employers the clarity and flexibility to invest in their employees’ futures.”

“With the SECURE 2.0 regulations in place, American families will be able to boost their savings and keep more of their hard-earned money through their automatic enrollment in a retirement account,” said IRS Chief Executive Officer Frank J. Bisignano. “These regulations reduce the administrative burden placed on taxpayers when making long-term financial decisions. More broadly, they further the IRS goal of improving taxpayer service by making interactions with the Service simpler and easier.”

STRENGTHENING AMERICANS’ RETIREMENT SAVINGS

The final regulations implement a key provision of the SECURE 2.0 Act by clarifying requirements for plan sponsors and simplifying certain participant notices. 

Covered retirement plans generally must automatically enroll eligible employees at a contribution rate of three percent. After an initial participation period, the default contribution rate must generally increase by at least one percentage point each year until it reaches at least ten percent, subject to a fifteen percent maximum. Employees may opt out or choose a different contribution rate. 

The final regulations generally apply to retirement plan years beginning after December 31, 2027, giving employers time to make necessary administrative changes. 

The final regulations:

  • Clarify statutory exceptions for qualifying small and new businesses, governmental plans, church plans, and SIMPLE 401(k) plans;
  • Give employers flexibility in the timing and amount of automatic contribution increases, within statutory limits;
  • Simplify plan communications by allowing certain required notices to be combined and reducing annual notice requirements for qualifying employees who are not participating, provided they receive annual reminders and any plan documents they are entitled to request; and
  • Explain how automatic enrollment requirements apply following plan mergers.

Press Release:            November 13, 2026

Contact:                     Treasury Public Affairs, Press@treasury.gov

Treasury Sanctions Guatemalan Drug Trafficking Organizations Supporting Mexican Narco-Terrorist Cartels

WASHINGTON — Today, the Department of the Treasury’s Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) sanctioned the Los Mendoza Drug Trafficking Organization (DTO) and the Los Huistas DTO for supporting Mexico’s largest narco-terrorist groups, the Sinaloa Cartel and Cartel de Jalisco Nueva Generacion (CJNG), which the Trump Administration has designated as both Foreign Terrorist Organizations (FTOs) and Specially Designated Global Terrorists (SDGTs) last year.  Based in Guatemala, Los Mendoza DTO and Los Huistas DTO control strategic trafficking corridors along the borders with Honduras and Mexico, making them indispensable logistics partners for the Sinaloa Cartel and CJNG.  

“Today’s action exposes the ties between politically influential Guatemalan criminal organizations and Mexican foreign terrorist organizations that facilitate the flow of deadly narcotics into the United States,” said Secretary of the Treasury Scott Bessent.  “Under President Trump’s America First agenda, the Treasury Department will continue to target the criminal networks that enable violent organizations like the Sinaloa Cartel and CJNG to traffic drugs across our borders and threaten the safety of the American people.”

The Los Mendoza DTO and Los Huistas DTO facilitate the receipt, storage, protection, and cross-border movement of narcotics destined for the United States and other international markets.  Through longstanding alliances spanning Central and South America, the Sinaloa Cartel and CJNG have expanded their criminal operations, established sophisticated cross-border trafficking networks, and consolidated control over critical segments of the illicit drug supply chain.  By targeting these key facilitators, OFAC is disrupting critical nodes in the supply chains that enable the trafficking of fentanyl, cocaine, methamphetamine, and other illicit drugs throughout the region. 

The action was taken pursuant to Executive Order (E.O.) 14059, which targets the international proliferation of illicit drugs and their means of production, and pursuant to E.O. 13224, as amended by E.O. 13886 (collectively, “E.O.13224, as amended”), which targets terrorists and their supporters. 

This action was done in coordination with the Department of State who is taking action against narcoterrorists destabilizing the Western Hemisphere.  In a concurrent action, the Department of State is also designating Los Lorenzanas as both an FTO pursuant to section 219 of the Immigration and Nationality Act, and as an SDGT pursuant to E.O. 13224, as amended.

SINALOA CARTEL AND CJNG: LEVERAGING GUATEMALAN ALLIANCES TO FACILITATE DRUG TRAFFICKING

Today, OFAC is sanctioning Los Mendoza DTO pursuant to E.O. 14059 and pursuant to E.O. 13224, as amended, for providing material support to the Sinaloa Cartel.  Additionally, OFAC is sanctioning Los Huistas DTO pursuant to E.O. 13224, as amended, for providing material support to the Sinaloa Cartel and CJNG.  In Guatemala, Los Mendoza DTO and Los Huistas DTO play important roles in facilitating narco-trafficking activities by controlling strategic trafficking corridors along the country’s borders with Honduras and Mexico.  The Sinaloa Cartel and CJNG collaborate with local criminal groups like Los Mendoza DTO and Los Huistas DTO to manage key logistical operations, including the receipt, storage, and cross-border transportation of narcotics, in order to move narcotics into Mexico for distribution in the United States and other international markets. 

The Sinaloa Cartel and CJNG are the most powerful cartels in Mexico and responsible for a significant portion of deadly drugs trafficked into the United States.  In addition to trafficking fentanyl, methamphetamine, cocaine, and other illicit drugs into the United States, these cartels have engaged in widespread violence and other criminal endeavors, such as fuel theft and timeshare fraud.  On February 20, 2025, the Department of State designated both the Sinaloa Cartel and CJNG as FTOs and SDGTs.  The Sinaloa Cartel and CJNG were each also identified by the United States as significant foreign narcotics traffickers on April 15, 2009 and on April 8, 2015, respectively, pursuant to the Foreign Narcotics Kingpin Designation Act. On December 15, 2021, OFAC also designated the Sinaloa Cartel and CJNG pursuant to E.O. 14059. 

LOS MENDOZA AND LOS HUISTAS DTOS – KEY LOGISTICS PARTNERS

Founded in the 1980s, Los Mendoza DTO is one of Guatemala’s oldest and most powerful criminal organizations.  The family-based organization operates as a key transportation and logistics intermediary for the Sinaloa Cartel, facilitating drug trafficking operations across Guatemala and Honduras.  Los Mendoza DTO supports the Sinaloa Cartel’s trafficking network by facilitating access to border crossings, clandestine airstrips, storage facilities, and local protection networks in the Guatemalan departments of San Marcos, Huehuetenango, and Peten.  Beyond narcotics trafficking, Los Mendoza DTO is involved in contract killings and money laundering, and has amassed significant economic interests through land dispossession, cattle ranching, agricultural businesses, and real estate investments across Peten, Izabal, and Guatemala’s border region with Mexico.

Active since the 1990s, Los Huistas DTO is one of Guatemala’s most powerful and longstanding criminal organizations.  Los Huistas DTO serves as a critical link in the cocaine trafficking supply chain from South America through Mexico and ultimately into the United States.  On March 18, 2022, OFAC designated Los Huistas DTO pursuant to E.O. 14059.  Los Huistas DTO maintains operational ties with both the Sinaloa Cartel and CJNG, providing logistical support and protection for narcotics shipments.  Los Huistas DTO’s longstanding ties to local businessmen, law enforcement officials, and politicians have enabled it to dominate the underworld in parts of northwestern Guatemala.  Through these relationships, Los Huistas DTO has cultivated political influence and institutional access which have facilitated its criminal operations and helped to shield the organization from the purview of law enforcement.

SANCTIONS IMPLICATIONS

As a result of today’s action, all property and interests in property of the designated persons described above that are in the United States or in the possession or control of U.S. persons are blocked and must be reported to OFAC.  In addition, any entities that are owned, directly or indirectly, individually or in the aggregate, 50 percent or more by one or more blocked persons are also blocked.  Unless authorized by a general or specific license issued by OFAC, or exempt, OFAC’s regulations generally prohibit all transactions by U.S. persons or within (or transiting) the United States that involve any property or interests in property of designated or otherwise blocked persons.

Violations of U.S. sanctions may result in the imposition of civil or criminal penalties on U.S. and foreign persons.  OFAC may impose civil penalties for sanctions violations on a strict liability basis.  OFAC’s Economic Sanctions Enforcement Guidelines provide more information regarding OFAC’s enforcement of U.S. economic sanctions.  In addition, financial institutions and other persons may risk exposure to sanctions for engaging in certain transactions or activities involving designated or otherwise blocked persons.  The prohibitions include the making of any contribution or provision of funds, goods, or services by, to, or for the benefit of any designated or blocked person, or the receipt of any contribution or provision of funds, goods, or services from any such person.  Non-U.S. persons are also prohibited from causing or conspiring to cause U.S. persons to wittingly or unwittingly violate U.S. sanctions, as well as engaging in conduct that evades U.S. sanctions.  Individuals located in the United States or abroad who provide information about sanctions violations to the Financial Crimes Enforcement Network’s (FinCEN’s) whistleblower incentive program may be eligible for awards if the information they provide leads to a successful enforcement action that results in monetary penalties exceeding $1,000,000.

Furthermore, engaging in certain transactions involving the persons designated today may risk the imposition of secondary sanctions on participating foreign financial institutions.  OFAC can prohibit or impose strict conditions on opening or maintaining, in the United States, a correspondent account or a payable-through account of a foreign financial institution that knowingly conducts or facilitates any significant transaction on behalf of a person who is designated pursuant to the relevant authority.

The power and integrity of OFAC sanctions derive not only from OFAC’s ability to designate and add persons to the Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List (SDN List), but also from its willingness to remove persons from the SDN List consistent with the law.  The ultimate goal of sanctions is not to punish, but to bring about a positive change in behavior.  For information concerning the process for seeking removal from an OFAC list, including the SDN List, or to submit a request, please refer to OFAC’s guidance on Filing a Petition for Removal from an OFAC List.

item.title: Remarks from Secretary of the Treasury Scott Bessent at the National Committee on U.S.-China Relations Gala
item.description:
U.S. Department of the Treasury

Office of Public Affairs

Press Release:            November 10, 2026

Contact:                     Treasury Public Affairs, Press@treasury.gov

Remarks from Secretary of the Treasury Scott Bessent at the National Committee on U.S.-China Relations Gala 

As prepared for delivery. 

Thank you, Evan [Greenberg], for that introduction, and for the invitation to be here. It gives me great pleasure to join you on this occasion.

More than as representatives of the world’s largest economies, we meet tonight as stewards of one of this century’s most consequential relationships.

Of course, when this Committee was formed in 1966, the Pacific was only the most visible distance between the United States and China. Formal diplomatic ties were still over a decade away. Our governments rarely spoke. And our people, likewise, rarely met.

But a “small, loosely cohesive” band of China watchers believed that distance was reason to know more, not less. And so, they set out to understand China more deeply and to engage with it more seriously. They could not anticipate where exactly the relationship would lead, only that it would matter.

The founders of this Committee set for themselves the ambitious task of reaching all segments of society—“from the layman, through the specialist, to the policy maker”—and “forging enduring links” between them.

Tonight, sixty years later, take one look around this room, and you can see how fully their ambition has been realized.

The United States and China represent different systems. Our national interests often diverge. But the links that you have built now bind generations and cultures together. They reach public servants and private citizens. Scholars who are bringing new ideas to light and entrepreneurs who are putting new ideas into practice.

On both sides of the Pacific, people understand each other better because the National Committee on U.S.-China Relations brought them together.

So, before I go any further, let me recognize two men who embody the best of this work.

Steve Orlins has devoted much of his professional life to the U.S.-China relationship. He was part of the team that established diplomatic relations in the 1970s and then spent decades strengthening the ties that sustain them. Steve, you leave behind a legacy of great consequence, for which I offer my sincere thanks and congratulations.

I am also pleased to acknowledge our second honoree. If Steve Orlins has shaped the history of our engagement with China, Stephen Schwarzman has made a transformative investment in its future. By founding the Schwarzman Scholars program, he has carried forward the conviction that animates this Committee. Relationships between nations are built on relationships between people. Steve, a new generation of leaders will be better prepared to navigate the U.S.-China relationship because you have given them the chance to understand it—and one another—more deeply. Congratulations.

Now, while this Committee has supported bilateral relations for decades, the truth is that the ties between us span centuries. In fact, our relationship with China is nearly as old as the republic itself.

In the winter of 1784, before we had a president—before we even had a constitution—an American ship, the Empress of China, departed New York Harbor and turned her bow toward the Pearl River.

The vessel carried American crew and cargo, and with them, the confidence of a young country that had won its independence and was already reaching for a place among the great trading nations of the world.

Major Samuel Shaw, who later served as the first American consul to China, recalled that upon the ship’s arrival, the Chinese people “were highly pleased at the prospect of so considerable a market for the productions of theirs.” Two nations, once separated by great distance, were drawn together by the possibilities of exchange.

So before Washington and Beijing had ambassadors, we had merchants.

Before our envoys learned how to engage, our people had already discovered how to do business.

And before diplomacy gave this relationship its shape, the flow of goods gave it its force.

Shaw celebrated that flow of commerce in both directions. And he was clear about the terms on which that commerce should proceed: “in all cases equal.” Even then, Americans expected a fair footing.

Nearly two and a half centuries have passed since the Empress made her maiden voyage.

What began with a single American ship bound for Canton—what began with the trading of ginseng for porcelain, tea, and silk—has matured into a vast trading network between the world’s two largest economies.

Of course, the world that Samuel Shaw inhabited has long receded into history. But the instinct that carried him across an ocean endures.

Americans still seek now what we sought then, which is to pursue opportunity wherever it lies, and to insist on fairness wherever we compete.

Trade must advance the interests of both parties without diminishing the sovereignty of either.

And it is precisely in that spirit that President Trump has approached our relationship with China.

Today, U.S.-China relations are defined by the relationship between our two leaders.

From the time of his first election, President Trump has, in his own words, “forged a friendship [with President Xi] built on mutual respect and the vital interests of our people.”

That friendship has brought unprecedented direct engagement between the leaders of our two nations, which I try to extend to the working level.

Of course, in May, President Trump traveled to Beijing. In September, President Xi came to Washington. And next week, I will join President Trump in Shenzhen, where the two leaders will meet before a fourth encounter in Miami.

These meetings are historic in their frequency. Never before have our leaders engaged face-to-face so often in a single year. But more significant is the understanding they are helping to establish.

President Trump and President Xi agree that the United States and China should build a constructive relationship on the basis of balance and reciprocity. And they’ve chartered two new institutions in service of those objectives.

Under the Board of Trade, we reached consensus to identify more favorable tariff treatment for $30 billion of non-sensitive goods in each direction. The board also launched a working group to address trade barriers in the agricultural sector. And previously, China agreed to import at least 25 million metric tons of soybeans and 10 million metric tons of coal from the United States over the next two years.

The Board of Investment, meanwhile, provides a structured forum for commercially meaningful issues, like market access for American companies and increased predictability for Chinese companies.

And these initiatives are part of our broader work to advance a fair and reciprocal relationship with China. They give practical expression to the principle at the core of President Trump’s agenda, which is to measure the success of American engagement abroad by what it delivers here at home. By how it advances the prosperity of our people. Strengthens the resilience of our economy. And safeguards the security of our nation.

Of course, the U.S. trade imbalance with China has long been a source of friction. And unlike a political class that tolerated China’s practices, President Trump has taken decisive steps to address them.

Let me state firmly and unequivocally tonight that as we work toward a more balanced relationship, our objective is to de-risk, not to decouple.

For decades, the American economy has grown too dependent on foreign supply, while China’s has become increasingly reliant on foreign demand. In other words, the United States must produce more of what we consume, while China must consume more of what it produces. Working together, we can strengthen both of our economies without perpetuating the imbalances between them.

As Ray Dalio would say, we should have a big, beautiful rebalancing.

So, as this President returns the American people to the center of American policy, let me be clear that our renewed emphasis on economic strength does not reflect hostility toward our trading partnerships. On the contrary, we are recovering the purpose that makes each of them worthwhile. After decades of imbalance, we are restoring a spirit of reciprocity for the benefit of both of our peoples.

Now, as we work together to address the great questions of the last century, we must also summon the resolve to answer those of the next.

In the final months of his life, Henry Kissinger was preoccupied with the challenges of a world he would not live to see. Even at the age of 100, his gaze, characteristically, was fixed on the future. On his last trip, he met with President Xi in Beijing to discuss deeper collaboration.

Kissinger had come to believe that the advent of superintelligence could represent a novel class of strategic danger. And he recognized that the obligation of great nations, even—and perhaps especially—those with profound differences, is to find common purpose.

So, at President Trump’s direction, we have begun that important work by establishing a new dialogue with China on SI, designed to guard against shared risks and prevent a misunderstanding between our two systems. We also expect to exchange best practices for evaluating and testing advanced models before their release, and for keeping human judgment firmly in command of this technology. Finally, we are establishing a direct channel to ensure that either nation can promptly alert the other to serious incidents involving its SI models.

As SI advances, so will the need to engage in new areas of risk management—and to demonstrate how two nations can reconcile the demands of competition with the responsibilities of leadership. As we do so, we should harbor no illusions about the differences between the United States and China. As I stated earlier, our interests will not always coincide. And our approach to every challenge, likewise, will not always converge.

Those early China watchers of the 1960s understood that the differences between our nations were too profound to ignore. But they also knew that the specter of our estrangement was too great to accept.

Generations of leaders have demonstrated their faith in the value of this relationship, dating back to when those enterprising merchants aboard the Empress of China returned to New York Harbor.

So I will take as my final words tonight those of Samuel Shaw, who, after a fourteen-month voyage, heralded “that a communication is thus happily opened between us and the Eastern Extreme of the Globe.”

The patriots of 1784 opened that passage through commerce. The statesmen of the 1970s widened it through diplomacy. And for six decades, the men and women of this Committee have sustained it through the patient work of bringing our people together.

Under President Trump, the United States will carry that work into a new era. We will enlarge the prospects for prosperity on both sides of the Pacific. And, secure in our own strength and unwavering commitment to the American people, we will honor those who first forged this relationship by renewing our resolve to strengthen it.

Thank you, and congratulations.

READOUT: Secretary of the Treasury Scott Bessent’s Call with China’s Vice Premier He Lifeng

WASHINGTON— Today, Secretary of the Treasury Scott Bessent and United States Trade Representative Jameison Greer spoke with Vice Premier He Lifeng of the People’s Republic of China to discuss the bilateral economic relationship and implementation of the Busan arrangement. The two officials reaffirmed the value of maintaining direct and candid communication.

Secretary Bessent emphasized the importance of China fully and immediately implementing its commitments made in Busan and raised concerns about recent Chinese actions. He underscored that continued progress depends on concrete results and that the United States will closely assess China’s implementation of the arrangement.

Secretary Bessent reiterated the Trump Administration’s commitment to pursuing trade and economic policies that benefit American workers, farmers, and businesses and strengthen U.S. economic and national security.
