item.title: Treasury Targets Global Scam Networks and the Corporate Infrastructure That Enables Them
item.description:
U.S. Department of the Treasury

Office of Public Affairs

Press Release:            November 5, 2026

Contact:                     Treasury Public Affairs, Press@Treasury.gov

Treasury Targets Global Scam Networks and the Corporate Infrastructure That Enables Them

WASHINGTON— Today, the U.S. Department of the Treasury’s Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) sanctioned four individuals and 41 entities that support the business network of Prince Group Transnational Criminal Organization (TCO) previously sanctioned by the United States for its role in cyber-enabled fraud, money laundering, and human trafficking.  Additionally, OFAC designated a Malaysian individual who defrauded U.S. victims by managing a network of Africa-based scammers.

“Cyber scam syndicates continue to steal billions of dollars from American victims while relying on sophisticated international business networks to launder their illicit proceeds,” said Secretary of the Treasury Scott Bessent. “Treasury remains committed to dismantling every layer of these organizations—from their leadership to the corporate structures and financial facilitators that enable them to operate with impunity.”

Today’s action builds on OFAC’s October 14, 2025 and June 23, 2026 designations targeting Prince Group leadership, affiliated companies, and financial facilitators. Prince Group TCO-affiliated actors have generated billions of dollars in illicit proceeds through sophisticated cyber-enabled fraud schemes, including digital asset investment scams, romance scams, and other online fraud that have victimized Americans and individuals around the world.  Many of these operations have been linked to scam compounds in Southeast Asia that rely on trafficked and coerced workers, while criminal proceeds are laundered through complex networks of offshore companies and financial facilitators.  The newly designated individuals and entities have helped sustain Prince Group TCO’s illicit global operations after the October 2025 and June 2026 designations by managing offshore corporate structures, concealing beneficial ownership, facilitating commercial activities, and providing administrative and financial services to senior Prince Group TCO executives.  Individuals targeted today have participated in activities to evade previous sanctions targeting the Prince Group TCO, including the transfer of property and owning of companies with or on behalf of previously designated Prince Group TCO leaders.  Today’s action further targets the corporate and financial infrastructure that has enabled Prince Group TCO leaders to conceal assets, evade prior sanctions, and maintain access to the international financial system. 

These actions are in furtherance of President Trump’s Executive Order (E.O.) 14390 of March 6, 2026, “Combating Cybercrime, Fraud, and Predatory Schemes Against American Citizens,” which orders the U.S. government to unleash every available tool to stop foreign-backed criminal networks that exploit vulnerable Americans through cybercrime, cyber-enabled fraud, and extortion. OFAC is designating 45 targets pursuant to E.O. 13581 (“Blocking Property of Transnational Criminal Organizations”), as amended by E.O. 13863 (“E.O. 13581, as amended”), and one target pursuant to E.O. 13694 (“Blocking the Property of Certain Persons Engaging in Significant Malicious Cyber-Enabled Activities”), as further amended by E.O. 13757, E.O. 14144, and E.O. 14306 (“E.O. 13694, as further amended”).

These actions are in coordination with the Federal Bureau of Investigation’s New York and Honolulu Field Offices, Department of Justice’s Scam Center Strike Force, and the U.S. Attorney’s office for the District of Alaska.  OFAC also appreciates the cooperation of the British Virgin Islands Financial Investigation Agency (BVI FIA) and the United Kingdom’s Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office (FCDO), whose timely assistance and information sharing were instrumental in supporting this sanctions action. 

TARGETING THOSE WHO EXPLOIT AMERICANS THROUGH FRAUD

Prince Group TCO-affiliated actors have targeted victims in the United States and around the world through sophisticated cyber-enabled fraud schemes, including digital asset investment scams, romance scams, and other online financial fraud.  These schemes rely on deception and social engineering to persuade victims to transfer funds or digital assets to criminally controlled accounts, generating billions of dollars in illicit proceeds.

Many of these operations are carried out from large-scale scam compounds in Southeast Asia, where trafficked and coerced workers are forced to perpetrate online fraud against victims across the globe.  Criminal proceeds are subsequently laundered through an international network of shell companies, offshore holding companies, financial facilitators, and digital asset transactions, allowing transnational criminal organizations to conceal the origin of illicit funds and integrate them into the legitimate financial system.

Today’s action builds on Treasury’s ongoing efforts to dismantle not only the leadership of these criminal enterprises, but also the overseas corporate infrastructure and professional facilitators that enable them to target American victims, move illicit proceeds across jurisdictions, and evade law enforcement.  The Prince Group TCO has developed an extensive network of companies spanning multiple jurisdictions to support its commercial interests and conceal assets connected to its criminal enterprise.  Rather than operating through a single corporate structure, senior Prince Group TCO executives have relied on layers of offshore holding companies, foreign entities, nominee directors, and corporate service providers to maintain control over assets while obscuring beneficial ownership.  Today’s designations target key components of that network, including companies and individuals that have facilitated corporate administration, managed offshore entities, and provided business services to senior Prince Group TCO officials.  These facilitators have played an important role in enabling the Prince Group TCO to access the international financial system and preserve the appearance of legitimate commercial activity.

DISMANTLING THE PRINCE GROUP'S CORPORATE INFRASTRUCTURE

Qiu Yong is a key Prince Group TCO member who controls multiple BVI and Hong Kong companies on behalf of Prince Group TCO, and who has served as an employee of a company controlled by Prince Group TCO’s leader, Chen Zhi.  Chen Zhi was designated on October 14, 2025.

Qiu Yong holds passports from multiple jurisdictions, including Cambodia, St. Lucia, and Türkiye, and is the beneficial owner of multiple BVI-based companies that control a network of Hong Kong companies involved in money lending and other business ventures.

Hong Kong-based companies Premium Financial Limited (Premium Financial) and Solar Scape Financial Limited (Solar Scape Financial) are money lending companies ultimately owned by Qiu Yong through BVI-registered Sun Speed Holdings Limited (Sun Speed Holdings) and Solar Scape Limited (Solar Scape), respectively.  Hong Kong-based Direct Astute HK Limited (Direct Astute HK) is ultimately owned by Qiu Yong via BVI-registered Direct Astute Limited (Direct Astute).  Hong Kong-based Glad Vast Limited (Glad Vast), Glad Sparkle Limited (Glad Sparkle), and Glad Harvest Limited (Glad Harvest) are linked to the wine industry and are ultimately owned by Qiu Yong through BVI-registered Glad Glory Limited (Glad Glory). Per Hong Kong media reporting, Qiu was involved in the distribution and sale of wine across Hong Kong and Macao, illustrating Prince Group TCO's reach into ostensibly legitimate businesses.  Qiu is also the beneficial owner of BVI-registered shelf companies Victory Flora Limited (Victora Flora), Win Applause Limited (Win Applause), Celestial Drive Limited (Celestial Drive), and Sino Sagacious Limited (Sino Sagacious).

Hong Kong-based Zhao Mengyao, a.k.a. Amy Zhao, is Qiu Yong’s personal assistant and serves as company secretary and co-director of multiple Hong Kong-based companies ultimately controlled by Qiu Yong.  Zhao Mengyao and Qiu Yong are both shareholders of Hong Kong-based Mighty Divine Trust Hong Kong Limited (Mighty Divine Trust), a company directed by Zhou Yun, an individual previously identified by OFAC as a financial assistant and wealth manager for Prince Group TCO leader Chen Zhi.  Mighty Divine Trust and Zhou Yun were both designated on October 14, 2025.

Qiu Yong is being designated pursuant to E.O. 13581, as amended, for having materially assisted, sponsored, or provided financial, material, or technological support for, or goods or services to or in support of, Prince Group TCO.  Premium Financial, Solar Scape Financial, Sun Speed Holdings, Solar Scape, Direct Astute HK, Direct Astute, Glad Vast, Glad Sparkle, Glad Harvest, Glad Glory, Victora Flora, Win Applause, Celestial Drive, and Sino Sagacious are being designated pursuant to E.O. 13581, as amended, for being owned or controlled by, or to having acted or purported to act for or on behalf of, directly or indirectly, Qiu Yong.   Zhao Mengyao is being designated pursuant to E.O. 13581, as amended, for having materially assisted, sponsored, or provided financial, material, or technological support for, or goods or services to or in support of, Qiu Yong.

OFAC is also targeting two individuals who are holding property for, or co-directing companies with, Prince Group TCO executive Chen Bo, who was designated on June 23, 2026. This includes Chen Bo’s wife, Cambodian national He Yujing, and Cambodian Prince Group TCO associate Visal Pang. Since OFAC’s action in October 2025, Chen Bo has transferred ownership of his Tokyo mansion to He Yujing, who also owns the Cambodian company Super Light Speed Kh Technology Co., Ltd.  Cambodia-based Visal Pang controls eleven Cambodian companies, several of which he co-directs with Chen Bo:  Cambodia First Unite Construction Group (CFU Group) Co., Ltd., First Unite International Logistics Co., Ltd., First Unite Networks Entertainment Co., Ltd., First Unite Property Co., Ltd., First Unite Decoration (Cambodia) Co., Ltd., Cambodian First Unite Construction Machinery Co., Ltd., Linkedus Technology Co., Ltd., Cambo Duty Free Merchandise Co., Ltd., Marco Polo Hotel Co., Ltd., U-Life Go Now Co., Ltd., and U-Life Kh Super App Co., Ltd.  Visal Pang was also designated by the United Kingdom on March 26, 2026.

Chen Bo remains in control of eleven Cambodian companies:  Asian Welfare Lotteries Co., Ltd., CB General Insurance PLC., Cambodian Resource Energy Development Co., Ltd., Cambodian Unite Wei Ye Investment Co., DT Zhi Zao, Co., Ltd., First Aquatic Industrial Co., Ltd., Mo Net Beauty Co., Ltd., Prince International Airlines Co., Ltd., Richeng Property Developer Co., Ltd., Tian Xu International Technology Plc., and ZHX Printing Equipment Cambodia Co., Ltd. He Yujing is being designated pursuant to E.O. 13581, as amended, for having materially assisted, sponsored, or provided financial, material, or technological support for, or goods or services to or in support of Prince Group TCO.  Super Light Speed Kh Technology Co., Ltd is being designated pursuant to E.O. 13581, as amended, for being owned or controlled by, or having acted or purported to act for or on behalf of, directly or indirectly, He Yujing.

Visal Pang is being designated pursuant to E.O. 13581, as amended, for having materially assisted, sponsored, or provided financial, material, or technological support for, or goods or services to or in support of Prince Group TCO.  Cambodia First Unite Construction Group (CFU Group) Co., Ltd., First Unite International Logistics Co., Ltd., First Unite Networks Entertainment Co., Ltd., First Unite Property Co., Ltd., First Unite Decoration (Cambodia) Co., Ltd., Cambodian First Unite Construction Machinery Co., Ltd., Linkedus Technology Co., Ltd., Cambo Duty Free Merchandise Co., Ltd., Marco Polo Hotel Co., Ltd., U-Life Go Now Co., Ltd., and U-Life Kh Super App Co., Ltd. are being designated pursuant to E.O. 13581, as amended, for being owned or controlled by, or having acted or purported to act for or on behalf of, directly or indirectly, Visal Pang.

Asian Welfare Lotteries Co., Ltd., CB General Insurance PLC., Cambodian Resource Energy Development Co., Ltd., Cambodian Unite Wei Ye Investment Co., DT Zhi Zao, Co., Ltd., First Aquatic Industrial Co., Ltd., Mo Net Beauty Co., Ltd., Prince International Airlines Co., Ltd., Richeng Property Developer Co., Ltd., Tian Xu International Technology Plc., and ZHX Printing Equipment Cambodia Co., Ltd. are being designated pursuant to E.O. 13581, as amended, for being owned or controlled by, or having acted or purported to act for or on behalf of, directly or indirectly, Chen Bo.

On June 23, 2026, OFAC designated Prince Group TCO associate Dai An, a high-level leader in the Prince Group TCO.  Dai is the majority owner of Singapore-based Chen Hua Holdings Pte Ltd (Chen Hua Holdings) and serves as director for Mauritius-based Meritwise Group Public Ltd (Meritwise Group) and Malaysia-based Greenmeadows Properties Sdn Bhd (Greenmeadows). 

Chen Hua Holdings, Meritwise Group, and Greenmeadows are being designated pursuant to E.O. 13581, as amended, for being owned or controlled by, or to have acted or purported to act for or on behalf of, directly or indirectly, Dai An.

Singapore-based Greenbay Multi Media Pte Ltd (Greenbay Multi Media) is 100 percent owned by OFAC-designated Prince Group TCO executive Thet Li.  Thet Li was designated by OFAC on October 14, 2025.

Greenbay Multi Media is being designated pursuant to E.O. 13581, as amended, for being owned or controlled by, or to have acted or purported to act for or on behalf of, directly or indirectly, Thet Li.

SANCTIONS AGAINST FACILITATOR OF MADAGASCAR-BASED SCAM NETWORK

Chui Kok Wa (Chui) led an extensive network of scammers located in Madagascar that targeted Americans with scams, including defrauding Americans of digital assets.  The scammers led by Chui exploited cyber-enabled technologies, including cryptocurrencies and digital systems and technologies, to defraud numerous Americans of over $400,000 equivalent, thereby materially contributing to the cybercrime and scam center threat to the national security, foreign policy, and economic health of the United States.  Chui’s network garnered sympathy from vulnerable victims in order to misappropriate their funds for the private financial gain of his network.  

OFAC is designating Chui Kok Wa pursuant to E.O. 13694, as further amended, for being responsible for or complicit in, or having engaged in, directly or indirectly, cyber-enabled activities originating from, or directed by persons located, in whole or in substantial part, outside the United States that are reasonably likely to result in, or have materially contributed to, a threat to the national security, foreign policy, or economic health or financial stability of the United States, and that have the purpose of or involve causing a misappropriation of funds or economic resources, intellectual property, proprietary or business confidential information, personal identifiers, or financial information for commercial or competitive advantage or private financial gain. 

SANCTIONS IMPLICATIONS 

As a result of today’s action, all property and interests in property of the designated persons described above that are in the United States or in the possession or control of U.S. persons are blocked and must be reported to OFAC.  In addition, any entities that are owned, directly or indirectly, individually or in the aggregate, 50 percent or more by one or more blocked persons are also blocked.  Unless authorized by a general or specific license issued by OFAC, or exempt, OFAC’s regulations generally prohibit all transactions by U.S.  persons or within (or transiting) the United States that involve any property or interests in property of designated or otherwise blocked persons.

Violations of U.S. sanctions may result in the imposition of civil or criminal penalties on U.S. and foreign persons.  OFAC may impose civil penalties for sanctions violations on a strict liability basis.  OFAC’s Economic Sanctions Enforcement Guidelines provide more information regarding OFAC’s enforcement of U.S. economic sanctions.  In addition, financial institutions and other persons may risk exposure to sanctions for engaging in certain transactions or activities involving designated or otherwise blocked persons. The prohibitions include the making of any contribution or provision of funds, goods, or services by, to, or for the benefit of any designated or blocked person, or the receipt of any contribution or provision of funds, goods, or services from any such person.  Non-U.S. persons are also prohibited from causing or conspiring to cause U.S. persons to wittingly or unwittingly violate U.S. sanctions, as well as engaging in conduct that evades U.S. sanctions.  Individuals located in the U.S. or abroad who provide information about sanctions violations to FinCEN’s whistleblower incentive program may be eligible for awards if the information they provide leads to a successful enforcement action that results in monetary penalties exceeding $1,000,000. 

The power and integrity of OFAC sanctions derive not only from OFAC’s ability to designate and add persons to the SDN List, but also from its willingness to remove persons from the SDN List consistent with the law.  The ultimate goal of sanctions is not to punish, but to bring about a positive change in behavior.  For information concerning the process for seeking removal from an OFAC list, including the SDN List, or to submit a request, please refer to OFAC’s guidance on Filing a Petition for Removal from an OFAC List.

U.S. Department of the Treasury

Office of Public Affairs

Contact:                     Treasury Public Affairs, Press@Treasury.gov

Treasury, IRS Announce Opportunity Zones Designations for Over 6,500 Communities Across America

The Working Families Tax Cuts Created a Permanent Process for States to Direct More Capital to Overlooked Communities 

WASHINGTON – The U.S. Department of the Treasury and the Internal Revenue Service (IRS) today announced the Qualified Opportunity Zone (QOZ) designations for all 50 states, territories, and the District of Columbia. 

 

Under President Trump’s Working Families Tax Cuts, the Opportunity Zone tax incentive was permanently renewed, enhanced incentives for investment in eligible rural communities were added, and a process was established for redesignating zones every ten years. The new QOZ designations will become effective on January 1, 2027, and retain this designation for ten years. 

 

“Under President Trump’s leadership, the Working Families Tax Cuts permanently renewed and strengthened Opportunity Zones, giving investors, entrepreneurs, and local leaders the long-term certainty they need to commit capital to communities that have been overlooked for too long,” said Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent. “Today’s announcement of the new designations will help direct private investment to communities that stand to benefit most, and expand economic opportunity, support job creation, and unlock long-term growth in these communities across the country.”

“Thanks to the leadership of President Trump, Qualified Opportunity Zones were permanently extended and expanded by the Working Families Tax Cuts giving states an opportunity to attract long-term investment into underserved, rural, and economically distressed areas,” said IRS Chief Executive Officer Frank J. Bisignano. “By designating thousands of new Qualified Opportunity Zones, the IRS and Treasury are enabling targeted investment and growth in communities where it is needed the most.”

BACKGROUND

 

Under President Trump’s Working Families Tax Cuts, the permanent renewal of the Opportunity Zone tax incentives, including enhanced incentives for investment in eligible rural communities, will continue to drive private investment in some of America’s most distressed communities. This builds on more than $110 billion in private-sector investment made since these tax incentives were established by the Tax Cuts and Jobs Act of 2017.

 

The full list and map of designated Opportunity Zones are available here.

 

On April 6, Treasury and the IRS released a list of 25,332 eligible census tracts across the country for nomination, of which 8,334 are in rural areas eligible for increased benefits as part of the Working Families Tax Cuts. On July 1, Treasury and the IRS began accepting nominations from Governors and the Mayor of the District of Columbia for eligible census tracts. An additional 130 eligible census tracts, of which 28 were in rural areas, were nominated during the statutory window. 

 

In total, 6,576 eligible census tracts were nominated by the end of the statutory window, of which 2,594 are in rural areas. All of the 6,576 eligible census tracts have been designated as QOZs effective January 1, 2027. Designation as a QOZ can help these 6,576 communities across the country attract new investment, create jobs, stimulate economic growth, and provide meaningful opportunities for residents.  

 

Additional information on nomination procedures was sent directly to the Governors and Mayor of the District of Columbia. The list of eligible census tracts is available here. The poverty rate and median family income for each tract can be found here.

item.title: Operation Economic Outcast Targets Global Maritime Fraud Network Supporting Iranian Regime
item.description:
U.S. Department of the Treasury

Office of Public Affairs

Press Release:            November 4, 2026

Contact:                     Treasury Public Affairs, Press@Treasury.gov

Operation Economic Outcast Targets Global Maritime Fraud Network Supporting Iranian Regime

Network Circumvented Maritime Law to Enable Iran’s Shadow Fleet

WASHINGTON—Today, as part of Operation Economic Outcast, the U.S. Department of the Treasury targeted the vast criminal network of India-based Suniel Kumar Sharma and his spouse, Jaspreet Preeti Shahid, who have supported Iran’s shadow fleet through a web maritime fraud. Their schemes have provided false flags and certifications to sanctioned vessels involved in transporting Iranian petroleum, including vessels operating on behalf of the Iranian military and its proxies.                                   

“As we have said many times, under Operation Economic Outcast, you are either with us or against us,” said Secretary of the Treasury Scott Bessent.  “We know where you are, and we will sanction those who continue supporting the Iranian regime, whether by land, sea, or air.”

False flags and fake maritime certifications allow vessels engaging in illicit activity to evade international regulations aimed at ensuring crew safety and safeguarding against environmental harm.  Falsely flagged vessels carry no valid protection and indemnity insurance, meaning that Iranian shadow fleet vessels operating under false flags could potentially cause billions of dollars in damages to the economies of the countries in whose territorial waters they operate.

OFAC today also sanctioned Türkiye-based Fugo Ground Services Inc for its ongoing services in support of Iran’s aviation sector. Treasury has repeatedly warned that it will take action against those who continue to support Iran’s aviation industry, a key enabler of the regime’s destabilizing proliferation and terrorist activity.

Concurrently with these designations, OFAC is issuing a new alert to industry to warn of the sanctions risks of dealing with potentially falsely flagged vessels, reemphasizing previous warnings from Treasury to the maritime industry to screen against unscrupulous actors such as Sharma and the vessels his network supports.  OFAC’s action also follows through on Treasury’s previous warning that any foreign firm or individual enabling sanctioned Iranian airlines—including through aircraft transfers, cargo services, or general sales agent support—will face serious consequences for supporting the world’s leading state sponsor of terrorism.  The designations imposed today are being taken pursuant to Executive Order (E.O.) 13902, which targets the Iranian petroleum, petrochemical, and aviation sectors, among other key sectors of the Iranian economy. 

OPERATION ECONOMIC OUTCAST IS ISOLATING THE IRANIAN REGIME

Announced by Secretary Bessent on August 24, 2026 and dubbed Economic D-Day, Operation Economic Outcast is severing the remaining economic lifelines that sustain the Iranian regime.  Treasury has mapped the networks, facilitators, and financial channels that Iran uses to smuggle oil, evade sanctions, and fund terror.  Working with partners across the U.S. government, the European Union, United Kingdom, Gulf partners, and others, Treasury is targeting any source of the regime’s illicit revenue, as well as its sanctions evasion schemes to move funds.  

Operation Economic Outcast significantly expanded sanctions risk for those who continue to choose to do business with Iran.  Treasury warned that any entity facilitating money laundering or sanctions evasion on behalf of Iran risks being cut off from the U.S. financial system. Operation Economic Outcast also expanded sanctions exposure for non-U.S. persons who continue doing business with the Iranian regime and will accelerate the pace of U.S. enforcement.  More information on Operation Economic Outcast is available here.

SHARMA CRIMINAL NETWORK

For years, Suniel Kumar Sharma (Sharma) and his wife, Jaspreet Preeti Shahid (Shahid), have, through their base in Chandigarh, India, defrauded maritime regulatory administrations in multiple jurisdictions in order to establish false flagging authorities and maritime classification societies.  Purporting to represent nations from nearly every continent, from Guyana to Eswatini and Laos, Sharma and Shahid have allowed the Iranian shadow fleet, including those operating on behalf of the Iranian military and its proxies, to evade international restrictions on their operation.

Sharma and Shahid’s operations began as early as 2014, when the couple sought to impersonate the flagging authority of the Caribbean nation of Dominica.  In 2023, Sharma established the Singapore-based Eswatini Maritime Affairs and International Ship Registry PTE. Ltd. (Eswatini Maritime), which, despite being publicly disavowed by Eswatini authorities, continues to provide flagging services for vessels transporting Iranian petroleum, including the sanctioned vessel PING SHUN (IMO 9231901), which at the time of its sanctioning had engaged in multiple shipments of Iranian oil.

Many of Sharma and Shahid’s false flagging registries are not tied to registered companies, however.  In each case, the Sharma network purchases web domains, creating websites that claim to offer a variety of services on behalf of a country that has not authorized it to provide any of those services.  The services often include flagging, seafarer training and certification, and vessel classification, all of which are traditionally handled by legitimate organizations that hold vessels to strict international standards.  

Sharma’s network can be tied to multiple active websites that purport to belong to legitimate flagging registries.  Among these false representations are websites purporting to provide flagging services on behalf of Aruba, Guyana, Mali, Mozambique, Malawi, Sint Maarten, and Timor-Leste, among others.  Sanctioned shadow fleet vessels have since gravitated towards these registries despite widespread awareness that they are not endorsed by the relevant governments.  For example, on April 22, 2026, the U.S. Department of War seized the false Guyana-flagged MAJESTIC X, formerly known as the PHONIX (IMO 9198317), which was carrying Iranian oil at the time of its boarding. 

Sharma and Shahid additionally manage a network of primarily India-based entities, some of which are used to establish fraudulent flagging registries.  Sharma is the managing director of India-based Oceaniek Technologies India, a company he has used to establish duplicitous flag registries, including those purporting to belong to Aruba, Nicaragua, and Sint Maarten.  Through these fraudulent registries Sharma has provided false flags to numerous sanctioned vessels that transport Iranian petroleum products, including LATTAFA (IMO 9245794), BINARY STAR (IMO 9380570), and VERA (IMO 9304655). 

As Sharma’s activities have garnered greater attention, Shahid has stepped in to manage—at least on paper—the pair’s business empire, which includes companies ranging from financial services businesses to media streaming platforms.  Following press coverage of his activities, Sharma has closed down multiple deceitful registries, including the Laos Ship Registry and Maritime Safety Administration, previously known as the International Maritime Safety Agency of Guyana, a company that served as a false flagging agency for Guyana and was likely intended to similarly impersonate the Laotian government.  

In addition to Shahid, Indian nationals Ashwani Kumar Dhiman and Ishwinder Singh nominally serve as directors of Sharma’s businesses, including India-based Aryavart Ship Management Private Limited.

Suniel Kumar Sharma is being designated pursuant to E.O. 13902 for operating in the petroleum sector of the Iranian economy.  Jaspreet Preeti Shahid is being designated pursuant to E.O. 13902 for having materially assisted, sponsored, or provided financial, material, or technological support for, or goods or services to or in support of, Suniel Kumar Sharma. 

Eswatini Maritime Affairs and International Ship Registry PTE. Ltd. is being designated pursuant to E.O. 13902 for being owned or controlled by, or having acted or purported to act for or on behalf of, directly or indirectly, Jaspreet Preeti Shahid. 

Oceaniek Technologies India is being designated pursuant to E.O. 13902 for being owned or controlled by, or having acted or purported to act for or on behalf of, directly or indirectly, Suniel Kumar Sharma. 

Aryavart Ship Management Private Limited is being designated pursuant to E.O. 13902 for being owned or controlled by, or having acted or purported to act for or on behalf of, directly or indirectly, Jaspreet Preeti Shahid.  Ashwani Kumar Dhiman and Ishwinder Singh are being designated pursuant to E.O. 13902 for having acted or purported to act for or on behalf of, directly or indirectly, Aryavart Ship Management Private Limited.

In addition, the following India-based companies are being designated pursuant to E.O. 13902 for being owned or controlled by, or having acted or purported to act for or on behalf of, directly or indirectly, Jaspreet Preeti Shahid:

  • Precept Trends Private Limited;
  • Polynesia Maritime Private Limited;
  • Alexarya Finserv Private Limited;
  • Alexarya Media and Entertainment Private Limited;
  • Viharaboating Private Limited; and
  • Aryavart Maritime and Educational Trust.

GROUND HANDLING COMPANY SUPPORTING IRANIAN AIRLINES

On August 24, 2026, Treasury issued determinations pursuant to E.O. 13902 against critical sectors––including aviation––that the Iranian regime uses to try to prop up its economy.  As Treasury has repeatedly highlighted, Iran uses its supposed “commercial” airlines, many of which are controlled by the regime and its military, to ferry fighters, ship weapons and sensitive technologies, and move gold and cash to its proxies.  Today, OFAC is taking action against a Türkiye-based ground handling company that continues to service sanctioned Iranian airlines, despite Treasury’s warnings of the sanctions risks associated with supporting Iran’s aviation sector. 

Türkiye-based Fugo Ground Services Inc provides ground handling and other services to several U.S.-designated Iranian airlines that continue to fly to Türkiye.  Fugo Ground Services Inc has direct service agreements with U.S.-sanctioned Iranian carriers including Iran Air Tour, Saha Airlines, Sepehran Airlines, Varesh Airlines, Taban Airlines, and Ata Airlines Company, and began providing services to several of these carriers in the weeks after their September 8, 2026 designations.

OFAC is designating Fugo Ground Services Inc pursuant to E.O. 13902 for operating in the aviation sector of the Iranian economy. 

SANCTIONS IMPLICATIONS

As a result of today’s action, all property and interests in property of the designated or blocked persons described above that are in the United States or in the possession or control of U.S. persons are blocked and must be reported to OFAC.  In addition, any entities that are owned, directly or indirectly, individually or in the aggregate, 50 percent or more by one or more blocked persons are also blocked.  OFAC’s regulations generally prohibit all transactions, unless authorized by a general or specific license issued by OFAC, or exempt, by U.S. persons or within (or transiting) the United States that involve any property or interests in property of blocked persons.

Violations of U.S. sanctions may result in the imposition of civil or criminal penalties on U.S. and foreign persons.  OFAC may impose civil penalties for sanctions violations on a strict liability basis.  OFAC’s Economic Sanctions Enforcement Guidelines provide more information regarding OFAC’s enforcement of U.S. economic sanctions.  The prohibitions include the making of any contribution or provision of funds, goods, or services by, to, or for the benefit of any designated or blocked person, or the receipt of any contribution or provision of funds, goods, or services from any such person.  Non-U.S. persons are also prohibited from causing U.S. persons to wittingly or unwittingly violate U.S. sanctions, as well as engaging in conduct that evades or conspires to violate U.S. sanctions.  Individuals located in the U.S. or abroad who provide information about sanctions violations to FinCEN’s whistleblower incentive program may be eligible for awards if the information they provide leads to a successful enforcement action that results in monetary penalties exceeding $1,000,000.  Financial institutions and other persons may risk exposure to sanctions for engaging in certain transactions or activities with designated or otherwise blocked persons, including the persons designated today.  This includes, in addition to blocking prohibitions, that OFAC can prohibit or impose strict conditions on opening or maintaining, in the United States, a correspondent account or a payable-through account of a foreign financial institution that knowingly conducts or facilitates any significant transaction on behalf of a person who is designated pursuant to the relevant authority.

The power and integrity of OFAC sanctions derive not only from OFAC’s ability to designate and add persons to the SDN List, but also from its willingness to remove persons from the SDN List, when consistent with relevant statutes and other authorities.  The ultimate goal of sanctions is to bring about a positive change in behavior.  What constitutes a sufficient change in circumstance will vary based on context, including the status of the broader geopolitical circumstances affecting the national security and foreign policy interests implicated by the declared national emergency.  In the case of sanctions related to Iran, OFAC is employing all available statutory, regulatory, and policy tools to resolve the persistent national emergencies posed by Iran, which has not changed its behavior to align with U.S. national security and foreign policy objectives.  OFAC sanctions determinations, including removal determinations, are made consistent with Administration foreign policy and national security policies and priorities.  For more information concerning the process for seeking removal from an OFAC list, including the SDN List, or to submit a request, please refer to OFAC’s guidance on How to Request Removal from an OFAC List.

Contact:                     Treasury Public Affairs, Press@treasury.gov

ICYMI: Secretary Bessent, Trump Administration Officials Announce New Fraud Prevention Measures in Minnesota

ST. CLOUD, Minn.—Today, U.S. Secretary of the Treasury Scott Bessent traveled to St. Cloud, Minnesota, along with Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) Director Kash Patel, Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) Administrator Dr. Mehmet Oz, Federal Trade Commission (FTC) Chairman Andrew Ferguson, and Assistant Attorney General for the National Fraud Enforcement Division Colin McDonald, to announce several initiatives to combat the rampant fraud that has wasted billions of taxpayer dollars in Minnesota. 

Today’s announcements underscore the Trump Administration’s coordinated efforts to protect taxpayer dollars, prevent fraud, and hold perpetrators accountable. Yesterday, FBI Minneapolis executed numerous search warrants related to ongoing fraud investigations in a combined 26-count indictment, and arrested four alleged Medicaid fraudsters who intended to defraud victims of over $41 million with actual losses amounting to $21.65 million. This was the outcome of an investigation by the FBI, IRS Criminal Investigation, U.S. Postal Inspection Service, and Homeland Security Investigations.

To further strengthen fraud prevention and detection, Treasury’s Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN) today issued an alert on risks involving cross-border payments through U.S.-based money services businesses after financial institutions reported more than $8 billion in potentially suspicious wire payments from 2021 to 2025. FinCEN also issued a notice to help financial institutions detect and report the exploitation of charities and nonprofits for terrorist financing, fraud, and other illicit activity. 

“President Trump has made clear that the war on fraud is not the work of one department, but a mandate we must carry across the Administration,” said Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent. “The U.S. Treasury is deploying every tool to bring an end to this egregious, unchecked fraud and hold perpetrators to account. And under this President’s leadership, wherever the money leads, the full weight of the federal government will follow.” Read Secretary Bessent’s op-ed in the Minnesota Star-Tribune.

“Our nation’s War on Fraud began in the Medicaid program right here in Minnesota. Since then, we’ve embarked on an unprecedented quest to crush corruption here and nationwide,” said CMS Administrator Dr. Mehmet Oz. “No society, no American, no patient should ever be the victim of the crimes we’ve seen since then. Fraudsters aren’t just stealing taxpayer dollars. they are threatening the quality, affordability, and integrity of the healthcare millions of Americans rely on.” 

“We’re identifying criminal funding streams, locating their center of gravity, and dismantling their networks across the country. That includes crushing the criminal fraud complex that has plagued America for so long,” said FBI Director Kash Patel. “The FBI is following the money, and if you steal from the government or American taxpayers, justice will find you."

“States such as Minnesota got a free pass for four full years. During this time, criminals were allowed to steal money from hardworking Americans and live a life of luxury while everyone else suffered,” said FTC Chairman Andrew Ferguson. “President Trump, Vice President Vance, and Secretary Bessent had a very clear message: Enough is enough. The era of robbing American citizens is over. We are putting Americans first again.”

“Minnesota is the epicenter for fraud in America,” said Acting Deputy Attorney General Trent McCotter for the Justice Department. “The Trump administration’s crackdown is working, and the results speak for themselves. Through the Minnesota Fraud Task Force we are systematically dismantling schemes preying on Americans. Backed by more than a thousand subpoenas and 40 warrants, the message is simple: No one stealing from taxpayer-funded programs is safe.”

“The alarming concentration of fraud targeting taxpayer-funded programs in Minnesota demands a coordinated and sustained response,” said Assistant Attorney General Colin M. McDonald of the Justice Department’s National Fraud Enforcement Division. “We are working with our law enforcement partners to uncover alleged fraud, protect public funds, and hold offenders accountable. We will continue these efforts until these schemes are dismantled and taxpayer dollars are protected from abuse in Minnesota.”

The full press conference is available to watch here.

item.title: Secretary Bessent, Senior U.S. Officials Announce New Fraud Prevention Measures in Minnesota
item.description:
U.S. Department of the Treasury

Office of Public Affairs

Press Release:            October 30, 2026

Contact:                     Treasury Public Affairs, Press@treasury.gov

Secretary Bessent, Senior U.S. Officials Announce New
Fraud Prevention Measures in Minnesota

Initiatives Aim to Stop Unchecked Fraud, Strengthen Accountability, and Restore
Integrity to the State

CLOUD, Minn.—In Minnesota, alongside other senior U.S. officials, U.S. Secretary of the Treasury Scott Bessent today announced several initiatives to combat the rampant fraud that has wasted billions of dollars in Minnesota. As part of the White House Task Force to Eliminate Fraud, Treasury continues to work tirelessly to protect American taxpayer dollars and restore integrity to federal benefits programs.

“When greed meets negligence, the American people suffer,” said Secretary of the Treasury Scott Bessent. “Under President Trump and Vice President Vance’s leadership, Treasury stopped nearly $190 million in funds tied to overseas fraud and returned more than $100 million to U.S. victims. We are working with the White House Task Force to Eliminate Fraud to help prevent this kind of abuse from happening again, in Minnesota or anywhere else.”

Secretary Bessent visited the Twin Cities earlier this year to announce several Treasury initiatives and investigations aimed at combating fraud in Minnesota. He met with representatives from financial institutions, fraud victims, state leaders, and affected community members. During that trip, Treasury also held training sessions for state and local law enforcement on detecting and investigating fraud. Treasury has continued to support federal, state, and local law enforcement with data that is essential to generating new leads, investigating fraud, and dismantling fraud schemes.

IRS-CI BRINGS ACCOUNTABILITY TO MINNESOTA

This week, Salim Said, co-conspirator in the Feeding Our Future fraud scheme that exploited a federally funded child nutrition program during the COVID-19 pandemic, was sentenced to 30 years in federal prison. These cases result from an investigation conducted by the FBI, IRS Criminal Investigation, U.S. Postal Inspection Service, and Homeland Security Investigations. Said was the owner of Safari Restaurant, which was utilized as an alleged food distribution site. As determined at trial, Said participated in a scheme to defraud the Federal Child Nutrition Program under the sponsorship of Feeding Our Future of $49 million. Said was convicted at trial on 21 counts related to wire fraud, money laundering, bribery and conspiracy.

FINCEN ALERTS FINANCIAL INSTITUTIONS TO RISKS OF CERTAIN CROSS-BORDER PAYMENTS INVOLVING MSBs

From 2021 to 2025, U.S. financial institutions reported more than $8 billion in potentially suspicious wire payments sent through U.S.-based money services businesses (MSBs) at the direction of foreign agents, which help facilitate transnational transactions.

Treasury’s Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN) today issued an alert asking financial institutions to watch for suspicious activity involving certain cross-border payments involving U.S. MSBs. Bad actors may exploit certain U.S. MSBs’ cross-border relationships to move funds through the U.S. financial system while obscuring the ultimate beneficiaries and the underlying purposes of transactions. These structures can help conceal illicit activity, such as funding for terrorist organizations.

FINCEN ISSUES NOTICE TO STOP ILLICIT ACTIVITY EXPLOITING CHARITIES AND NON-PROFITS

FinCEN today also issued a notice to help financial institutions detect and report suspicious activity involving the exploitation of charities and non-profit organizations. Fraudsters sometimes exploit the fundraising capabilities of charities and non-profit organizations to facilitate terrorist financing, fraud, and other illicit activity. Bad actors may funnel funds to terrorists, divert taxpayer dollars from government programs, and steal money intended for charitable causes.

The notice describes three types of schemes exploiting charities and non-profit organizations:

  • sham charities, which involve bad actors falsely advertising a legitimate purpose for a charity or non-profit organization but using funds for illicit activity (including terrorism);
  • fraud schemes, which involve bad actors falsely advertising a legitimate purpose for a charity or non-profit organization but using funds to support their lifestyle; and
  • embezzlement, which involves insiders abusing their position of trust at a legitimate charity or non-profit organization to steal money.

MATERIALS

  • Alert on Risks Associated with Foreign-Agent-Directed Transactions
  • Notice on the Use of Charities and Non-Profit Organizations for Illicit Activity

item.title: Treasury Sanctions Facilitators of DPRK IT Worker Fraud Targeting U.S. Businesses
item.description:
U.S. Department of the Treasury

Office of Public Affairs

Press Release:            October 28, 2026

Contact:                     Treasury Public Affairs, Press@treasury.gov

Treasury Sanctions Facilitators of DPRK IT Worker Fraud Targeting

U.S. Businesses

WASHINGTON— Today, the U.S. Department of the Treasury’s Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) sanctioned 10 individuals and one entity for their roles in Democratic People’s Republic of Korea (DPRK) government-run information technology (IT) worker schemes that defraud U.S. businesses and generate revenue for the DPRK’s unlawful weapons of mass destruction (WMD) and ballistic missile programs.

“The North Korean regime continues targeting and exploiting American companies through fraudulent activities conducted by its overseas IT operatives, who weaponize sensitive data and extort businesses for substantial payments,” said Secretary of the Treasury Scott Bessent. “Under President Trump’s leadership, Treasury will continue to use all available tools to protect U.S. businesses from these malicious activities and hold those responsible accountable.” The DPRK continues to rely on fraudulent documents, stolen identities, and fabricated personas to conceal its IT workers and secure employment with legitimate companies, including those in the United States and allied countries.  

The DPRK regime then appropriates most of these workers’ wages, generating hundreds of millions of dollars to fund its unlawful WMD and ballistic missile programs.  Today’s action targets key facilitators and financial networks that help sustain these schemes and move illicit proceeds on behalf of the DPRK.  These networks have leveraged sophisticated cryptocurrency transactions, money laundering techniques, and emerging technologies, including artificial intelligence tools, to generate and transfer millions of dollars for the DPRK government.  In addition to generating revenue, DPRK IT workers have exploited their access to corporate networks to deploy malware, exfiltrate sensitive data, and steal proprietary information, creating significant risks for businesses worldwide.

Today’s action builds on OFAC’s March 12, 2026 designation of a separate DPRK IT worker network and demonstrates Treasury’s sustained commitment to dismantling the networks that generate illicit revenue for the DPRK.  These networks permeate through the global financial system, necessitating a unified response to match the threat.  The United States is joined this month by Australia and the European Union in designating individuals and entities supporting the DPRK’s revenue generation and military activities.  Treasury continues to take these actions in close partnership with the Multilateral Sanctions Monitoring Team (MSMT) Participating States and other international partners.  Working with allies and partners, the United States will continue to expose and disrupt those enabling the DPRK to evade sanctions and finance its unlawful weapons programs. 

More information about the tactics utilized by DPRK IT workers and steps that can be taken to protect private networks can be found in advisories and alerts regarding DPRK IT workers issued by the Departments of State, Treasury, and Justice; the FBI; and a multilateral consortium of law enforcement.

KEY ENABLERS OF GLOBAL DPRK IT WORKER NETWORKS

OFAC’s action today targets several DPRK IT worker networks by designating facilitators and DPRK IT workers based in the DPRK and Russia.

Vitold Viktorovich Obertas (Obertas) is a Russian intermediary for illicit DPRK financial transactions, including for Amnokgang Technology Development Company (Amnokgang).  OFAC designated Amnokgang in its March 12, 2026 action.  Since January 2025, Obertas has conducted nearly $2 million worth of cryptocurrency conversions, as well as at least $1.25 million in other currency transactions, for DPRK officials.  OFAC is designating Obertas pursuant to Executive Order (E.O.) 13687 for having materially assisted, sponsored, or provided financial, material, or technological support for, or goods or services to or in support of, the Government of North Korea.   

DPRK-national Limited Liability Company Alis (Alis) lead Kim Ki Hyok leads a Russia-based delegation of DPRK IT workers, whose primary duties include monitoring Alis IT workers and ensuring they meet their financial targets.  OFAC designated Alis in March 2024 for being subordinate to the Chinyong Information Technology Cooperation Company (Chinyong), which OFAC designated in May 2023.  Since 2024, Kim Ki Hyok has transferred cryptocurrency for the delegation valued at nearly $500,000.  Additionally, DPRK national Kim Hyo Dong leads a separate Russia-based Chinyong-subordinate delegation.  Since at least December 2023 Kim Hyo Dong has provided logistical assistance to the IT worker delegation, engaged in sanctions evasion efforts, and facilitated the transfer of over $100,000 equivalent in financial assets.  OFAC is designating Kim Ki Hyok and Kim Hyo Dong pursuant to E.O. 13687 for having materially assisted, sponsored, or provided financial, material, or technological support for, or goods or services to or in support of, Chinyong.

Since 2024, Russian national Ilya Aleksandrovich Boykov (Boykov) has actively supported Alis by exchanging and converting an equivalent of $3.5 million in cryptocurrency transactions, monitoring cryptocurrency transactions, and providing logistical support for Alis.  OFAC is designating Boykov pursuant to E.O. 13687 for having materially assisted, sponsored, or provided financial, material, or technological support for, or goods or services to or in support of, Alis. 

Since at least 2024, the First Financial and Technical Development Center (FFTDC) is a DPRK-controlled entity located in Russia that uses DPRK IT workers who have generated several millions of dollars on behalf of the DPRK government.  The FFTDC has deployed several highly trained DPRK IT workers to Russia who employ Super Intelligence (SI) tools and use sophisticated money laundering methods, including complex cryptocurrency transfers, to facilitate their revenue generation schemes.  Since 2025, Russia-based DPRK IT workers Kim Kyong Ju, Ri Thae Chol, So Hyon Jin, Han Yu Song, Kim Sung Gwan, and Hyon Se Il have collectively generated over $750,000 on behalf of the FFTDC.   

OFAC is designating FFTDC pursuant to E.O. 13722 for having engaged in, facilitated, or been responsible for the exportation of workers from North Korea, including exportation to generate revenue for the Government of North Korea or the Workers’ Party of Korea.  Additionally, OFAC is designating Kim Kyong Ju, Ri Thae Chol, So Hyon Jin, Han Yu Song, Kim Sung Gwan, and Hyon Se Il pursuant to E.O. 13722 for having materially assisted, sponsored, or provided financial, material, or technological support for, or goods or services to or in support of, FFTDC.    

SANCTIONS IMPLICATIONS

As a result of today’s action, all property and interests in property of the designated or blocked persons described above that are in the United States or in the possession or control of U.S. persons are blocked and must be reported to OFAC.  In addition, any entities that are owned, directly or indirectly, individually or in the aggregate, 50 percent or more by one or more blocked persons are also blocked.  Unless authorized by a general or specific license issued by OFAC, or exempt, OFAC’s regulations generally prohibit all transactions by U.S. persons or within (or transiting) the United States that involve any property or interests in property of designated or otherwise blocked persons.

Violations of U.S. sanctions may result in the imposition of civil or criminal penalties on U.S. and foreign persons.  OFAC may impose civil penalties for sanctions violations on a strict liability basis.  OFAC’s Economic Sanctions Enforcement Guidelines provide more information regarding OFAC’s enforcement of U.S. economic sanctions.  In addition, financial institutions and other persons may risk exposure to sanctions for engaging in certain transactions or activities involving designated or otherwise blocked persons.  The prohibitions include the making of any contribution or provision of funds, goods, or services by, to, or for the benefit of any designated or blocked person, or the receipt of any contribution or provision of funds, goods, or services from any such person.  Non-U.S. persons are also prohibited from causing or conspiring to cause U.S. persons to wittingly or unwittingly violate U.S. sanctions, as well as engaging in conduct that evades U.S. sanctions.  Individuals located in the U.S. or abroad who provide information about sanctions violations to Treasury’s Financial Crimes Enforcement Network’s whistleblower incentive program may be eligible for awards if the information they provide leads to a successful enforcement action that results in monetary penalties exceeding $1,000,000. 

Furthermore, engaging in certain transactions involving the persons designated today may risk the imposition of secondary sanctions on participating foreign financial institutions.  OFAC can prohibit or impose strict conditions on opening or maintaining, in the United States, a correspondent account or a payable-through account of a foreign financial institution that knowingly conducts or facilitates any significant transaction on behalf of a person who is designated pursuant to the relevant authority.

The power and integrity of OFAC sanctions derive not only from OFAC’s ability to designate and add persons to the List of Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons (the “SDN List”), but also from its willingness to remove persons from the SDN List consistent with the law.  The ultimate goal of sanctions is not to punish, but to bring about a positive change in behavior.  For information concerning the process for seeking removal from an OFAC list, including the SDN List, or to submit a request, please refer to OFAC’s guidance on Filing a Petition for Removal from an OFAC List.

item.title: Treasury Sanctions Rwandan Ministry of Defence and Financial Institution Supporting M23
item.description:
U.S. Department of the Treasury

Office of Public Affairs

Press Release:            October 28, 2026

Contact:                     Treasury Public Affairs, Press@treasury.gov

Treasury Sanctions Rwandan Ministry of Defence and
Financial Institution Supporting M23

WASHINGTON— Today, the U.S. Department of the Treasury’s Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) imposed sanctions on the Rwandan Ministry of Defence and Zigama Credit and Savings Society, a Rwandan financial institution that has played a key role in facilitating Rwanda’s support for the March 23 Movement (M23) and its political wing, the Congo River Alliance. 

“Today, the United States makes good on President Trump’s promise to hold Rwanda accountable for its commitments under the Washington Accords for Peace and Prosperity,” said Secretary of the Treasury Scott Bessent.  “Rwanda must halt its support for M23 and withdraw its troops from eastern DRC.”

On October 12, the Front for the Refoundation of the Nation announced its formation as the successor to the Congo River Alliance.  M23 is a U.S.- and United Nations-designated armed group that has illegally seized territory in eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC).  With support from Rwanda’s security apparatus, including the deployment of thousands of troops and provision of military equipment, logistics, and training, M23 has captured key population centers and mining areas in eastern DRC, where it has perpetrated human rights abuses, subjected civilians to exploitation and forced labor, and contributed to a severe humanitarian crisis marked by mass displacement.

The historic U.S.-brokered Washington Accords for Peace and Prosperity (Washington Accords) were signed by the DRC and Rwandan heads of state on December 4, 2025.  In addition to paving the way for a peaceful resolution to the conflict in eastern DRC, the Washington Accords incorporated a regional economic framework to expand trade and investment, enhance transparency in critical minerals supply chains, and promote greater investment in the Great Lakes Region of Africa.

THE RWANDAN MINISTRY OF DEFENCE: ENABLING REBELLION IN EASTERN DRC

The Rwandan Ministry of Defence (Rwandan MoD) is the umbrella organization for Rwanda’s security services, including the Rwanda Defence Force (RDF), which OFAC sanctioned on March 2, 2026.  At the direction of the Rwandan MoD, the RDF has deployed thousands of troops across eastern DRC’s North and South Kivu provinces, where they conduct operations alongside M23 and provide the armed group with military equipment, supplies, logistical support, and training.  The RDF has also introduced advanced weaponry to the battlefield, including surface to air missile systems and jamming equipment, creating risks for civilian aviation in eastern DRC.

Since its rebellion reemerged in 2021, M23 has carried out extrajudicial killings, unlawful detentions, and torture or other physical abuses in areas under its control.  In early 2025, M23 captured Goma and Bukavu, the provincial capitals of North and South Kivu provinces, respectively.  M23 has also taken control of mining areas in eastern DRC, including gold mines in South Kivu province and Rubaya, an expansive area for coltan mining in North Kivu province.  In M23-controlled mining areas, civilians have been subjected to forced labor, dangerous working conditions, and illegal “taxation” schemes.  Minerals sourced from M23-controlled territory are integrated into supply chains in Rwanda, whose domestic mining capacity is smaller than export volumes reported since M23’s rebellion began.  On July 8, 2024, the U.S. Department of State issued a statement of concern related to mineral supply chains that contribute to ongoing instability in eastern DRC.

The Rwandan MoD is being designated pursuant to E.O. 13413, as amended, for having materially assisted, sponsored, or provided financial, material, logistical, or technological support for, or goods or services in support of the RDF.

ZIGAMA: FINANCING REBELLION, PARTICIPATING IN MINERALS SMUGGLING

Zigama Credit and Savings Society (Zigama) is a Rwandan financial institution that operates on behalf of Rwanda’s security services.  Zigama has facilitated payments to entities in China and additional countries for weapons, ammunition, and other military equipment for the RDF.  Zigama has also facilitated payments for RDF travel and accommodation for training activities.

As Treasury highlighted in a previous designation, the RDF and M23 control gold mining sites in South Kivu province.  Following the removal of gold from these sites, Rwandan government forces have maintained strict oversight of the gold.  A Zigama branch enabled the transportation of gold sourced from M23-controlled territory in eastern DRC to Kigali.  In addition, Zigama has facilitated financial transactions for M23 and the Congo River Alliance, amounting to tens of millions of dollars.

Zigama is being designated pursuant to E.O. 13413, as amended, for having materially assisted, sponsored, or provided financial, material, logistical, or technological support for, or goods or services in support of, the RDF, M23, and the Congo River Alliance.
